Program the appropriate presentation time control (supported recovery modes "0001 - 0011") to the EMAC\_PPS\_CTL.PPSCTRL\_PPSCMD bit field (for 0th instance) and EMAC\_PPS\_CTL.PPSCMD1 through EMAC\_PPS\_CTL.PPSCMD3 bits. Program all the EMAC\_PPS\_CTL.MCGREN0 through EMAC\_PPS\_CTL.MCGREN3 bits to enable MCGR mode.
4. For instances enabled for media clock recovery, the corresponding EMAC\_MCGR[n] trigger signal is set by the EMAC. For every request generated by EMAC, program the target presentation time into the EMAC\_PPS[n]\_TGTM\_SEC register and acknowledge the request by asserting the corresponding trigger completer signal. Acknowledgment can be given before/after programming the target presentation time.
5. Observe the recovered media clock on the corresponding EMAC\_PTPPPS[n] pin.

## EMAC Programming Concepts

The following sections provide basic information and guidelines to help with programming the EMAC module.

## IEEE 802.3 Ethernet Packet Structure

The IEEE 802.3 Frame Structure table provides typical frame format of an Ethernet packet. Refer to the IEEE standards for detailed information on Ethernet packets and their format.

Table 28-109: IEEE 802.3 Frame Structure

| Parameter   | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |   Position in Ether- net Packet | Total Bytes   |
|-------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------|---------------|
| PREAMBLE    | This parameter is a 56-bit (7-byte) pattern of alternating 1 and 0 bits (#10101010), which allows devices on the network to detect a new incoming frame for synchronization.                                                                                                                          |                               1 | 7             |
| SFD         | The SFD (#10101011) is a 1-byte pattern designed to break the preamble pattern, and signal the start of the actual frame.                                                                                                                                                                             |                               2 | 1             |
| DA          | 48-bit destination address. This parameter can be a unicast, multicast, or broadcast address.                                                                                                                                                                                                         |                               3 | 6             |
| SA          | 48-bit long source address, typically a unicast, multicast, or broadcast address.                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |                               4 | 6             |
| LT          | Typically this field is the length, in terms of the number of bytes, and can be anywhere between 0-1500. When the value is greater than or equal to 0x0600, this field also indicates the type of special payload carried by the frame. Examples include 0x8808 for flow control and 0x0800 for IPv4. |                               5 | 2             |
| DATA        | Actual application data payload, usually between 0-1500.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |                               6 | 0-1500        |
| PAD         | This field compensates for data frames that are shorter than 64 bytes long, not including the preamble.                                                                                                                                                                                               |                               7 | 0-46          |
| FCS         | The frame check sequence is a 32-bit cyclic redundancy check that detects corrupted data within the entire frame. This parameter is generated from a CRC-32 polynomial code (CRC-32-IEEE): G (x) = x32 + x26 + x23 + x22 + x16 + x12 + x11 + x10 + x8 + x7 + x5 + x4 + x2 + x + 1.                    |                               8 | 4             |

## Frame Size Statistics for Application Software

Table 28-110: Ethernet Frame Size Statistics

| Frame size statistics        | VLAN-specific change Comments                                                                       |                                                                             |
|------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Information bytes/Header     | 4 byte 802.1Q header inserted after source address and before Type/LAN in 802.3 packets = 22 bytes. | 6 x 2 + 2 + 4 = 18 bytes (DA+SA+LT+FCS)                                     |
| Minimum Frame Size (typical) | If DATA is NULL, 42-byte padding makes 64 bytes (42 +22)                                            | 64 bytes. If DATA is NULL, 46-byte padding makes 64 bytes (46 +18)          |
| Maximum Frame Size (typical) | 1522 bytes                                                                                          | 1518 bytes (1500 bytes DATA and 18-bytes header)                            |
| Jumbo Frame Size             | 9022 bytes                                                                                          | Typical industry standard. Ethernet jumbo frame size treated as 9018 bytes. |

The Visualization of Programmable Packet Size table provides the byte sizes of packets with various configurations.

Table 28-111: Visualization of Programmable Packet Size

| Size in Bytes   | Comments                                                                          |
|-----------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 16384           | Receive watchdog and transmit jabber disabled, jumbo frames enabled.              |
| 10240           | Receive watchdog and transmit jabber disabled, jumbo frames disabled.             |
| 2048            | Receive watchdog and transmit jabber enabled.                                     |
| 1518            | Typical max size of Ethernet frame. Receive watchdog and transmit jabber enabled. |
| 64              | Typical minimum size of Ethernet frame.                                           |
| < 64            | Runt frames requiring Zero-PAD.                                                   |

## Ethernet Packet Structure in C

The following is an example for Ethernet packet structure in the C language.

```
typedef struct ETHER_PACKET { char  dst_addr[6];             //destination address char  src_addr[6];             //source address char  length[2];               //length of actual data char  data[DATA_SIZE];         //application data char  fdlimit[DELIMIT_SIZE];   //32-bit delimit (if manual appending) char  fcs[4];                  //crc frame checksum, used by RX buffer. } ETHER_PACKET;
```

## PTP Header Structure in C

The following code is an example of the PTP message format.

```
/* PTP Message Format (Refer to PTP Frame Over IPv4)*/ typedef struct EMAC_PTP_HEADER { unsigned char    messageType:4,    //PTP Version 2 message type transportSpecific:4; unsigned char    versionPTP;       //PTP Version (1 or 2) unsigned short    messageLength; unsigned char    domainNumber; unsigned char    RESERVED1; unsigned short    flagField; unsigned char    correctionField[8]; unsigned char    RESERVED2[4]; unsigned char    sourcePortIdentity[10]; unsigned short    sequenceid; unsigned char    controlField;     //PTP Version 1 message type unsigned char    logMessageInterval; }EMAC_PTP_HEADER;
```

## DMA Channel n Control Register

The EMAC\_DMA[n]\_CTL register specifies the MSS value for segmentation, length to skip between two descriptors, and also the features such as header splitting and 8xPBL mode.

Figure 28-58: EMAC\_DMA[n]\_CTL Register Diagram

![Image](31_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_(EMAC)_artifacts/image_000057_fb644a79a7c30cc3dbd5eaf0c2b0edc637a6eda23eada7a4a2ad8db5f9d4e60f.png)

Table 28-113: EMAC\_DMA[n]\_CTL Register Fields

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
|--------------------|------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 24 (R/W)           | SPH        | Split Headers. When the EMAC_DMA[n]_CTL.SPH bit is set (=1), the DMAsplits the header and payload in the receive path. The DMAwrites the header to Buffer Address1 of RDES0. The DMAwrites the payload to the buffer to which the Buffer Address2 is pointing. The software must ensure that the header fits into the receive buffers. If the header length exceeds the receive buffer size, the DMAdoes not split the header and payload. The EMAC_DMA[n]_CTL.SPH bit is available only when the split header feature is enabled (EMAC_HW_FTR_PSNT1.SPHEN =1). 0 Split Headers Feature is Disabled |
| 20:18 (R/W)        | DSL        | Descriptor Skip Length. The EMAC_DMA[n]_CTL.DSL bit specifies the number of 32-bit words to skip between two unchained descriptors. The address skipping starts from the end of the current descriptor to the start of the next descriptor. When EMAC_DMA[n]_CTL.DSL = 0, the DMAtakes the descriptor table as con- tiguous.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |

Table 28-113: EMAC\_DMA[n]\_CTL Register Fields (Continued)

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
|--------------------|------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 16 (R/W)           | PBLX8      | 8xPBL Mode. When the EMAC_DMA[n]_CTL.PBLX8 bit is set, the PBL value pro- grammed in bits[21:16] in EMAC_DMA[n]_TXCTL and bits[21:16] in EMAC_DMA[n]_RXCTL is multiplied by eight times. Therefore, the DMAtransfers the data in 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, and 256 beats depending on the PBL value. 0 8xPBL Mode is Disabled                                 |
| 13:0 (R/W)         | MSS        | Maximum Segment Size. The EMAC_DMA[n]_CTL.MSS field specifies the maximum segment size to be used while segmenting the packet. The EMAC_DMA[n]_CTL.MSS field is valid only when EMAC_DMA[n]_TXCTL.TSE =1. The value programmed in this field must be more than the configured data width in bytes. Use a EMAC_DMA[n]_CTL.MSS value of 64 bytes or more. |

## DMA Channel n Missed Frame Counter Register

The EMAC\_DMA[n]\_MISSFRM\_CNT register indicates the number of frames that the DMA dropped due to a bus error or due to programming the EMAC\_DMA[n]\_RXCTL.RPF bit.

Figure 28-64: EMAC\_DMA[n]\_MISSFRM\_CNT Register Diagram

![Image](31_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_(EMAC)_artifacts/image_000063_598302dc9419cb5bf707372a495ddb00aae7181e125a7814b8f4a2374b31020a.png)

Table 28-119: EMAC\_DMA[n]\_MISSFRM\_CNT Register Fields

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
|--------------------|------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 15 (R/NW)          | MFCO       | Overflow Status of the MFC Counter. When EMAC_DMA[n]_MISSFRM_CNT.MFCO bit is set (=1), the MFC counter does not get incremented further. The bit is cleared (=0) when this register is read. Access restriction applies. Clears on read. Self-set to 1 on internal event.                                                                      |
| 10:0 (R/NW)        | MFC        | Dropped Packet Counters. The EMAC_DMA[n]_MISSFRM_CNT.MFC field indicates the number of frames that are dropped by the DMAeither because of a bus error or because of programing the EMAC_DMA[n]_RXCTL.RPF bit. The counter is cleared when this register is read. Access restriction applies. Clears on read. Self-set to 1 on internal event. |

## DMA Channel n Receive Descriptor List Address Register

The EMAC\_DMA[n]\_RXDSC\_ADDR register points the DMA to the start of the receive descriptor list.

The descriptor lists reside in the physical memory space of the application. It must be 32-bit aligned. The DMA internally converts it to bus width aligned address by making the corresponding least significant bits low.

Writing to the EMAC\_DMA[n]\_RXDSC\_ADDR register is permitted only when reception is stopped. When stopped, this register must be written to before the receive start command is given.

Write to this register only when Rx DMA has stopped (EMAC\_DMA[n]\_RXCTL.SR = 0). When stopped, this register can be written with a new descriptor list address.

When EMAC\_DMA[n]\_RXCTL.SR = 1, the DMA takes the newly programmed descriptor base address.

Figure 28-65: EMAC\_DMA[n]\_RXDSC\_ADDR Register Diagram

![Image](31_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_(EMAC)_artifacts/image_000064_35f5a92857e3734ac644a0ec51e3ed74ecd27dcab232b8910a38f8907d19fce4.png)

Table 28-120: EMAC\_DMA[n]\_RXDSC\_ADDR Register Fields

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
|--------------------|------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 31:2               | RDESLA     | Start of Receive List. The EMAC_DMA[n]_RXDSC_ADDR.RDESLA field contains the base address of the first descriptor in the Rx descriptor list. The DMAignores the last two bits (1:0) and internally takes these bits as all-zero. Therefore, these LSB bits are read-only (RO). |
| (R/W)              |            |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |

## DMA Channel n Receive Descriptor Tail Pointer Register

The EMAC\_DMA[n]\_RXDSC\_TLPTR register indicates an offset from the base and indicates the location of the last valid descriptor.

Figure 28-66: EMAC\_DMA[n]\_RXDSC\_TLPTR Register Diagram

![Image](31_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_(EMAC)_artifacts/image_000065_bfe4d6c3da59129658b341cdda75e709fe18466a6d6da29063a997cef9ba2dbf.png)

The software writes the tail pointer to add more descriptors to the Rx channel. The hardware tries to write all received packets to the descriptors referenced between the head and the tail pointer registers. |

## DMA Channel n Receive Control Register

The EMAC\_DMA[n]\_RXCTL register controls the Rx features such as PBL, buffer size, and extended status.

Figure 28-67: EMAC\_DMA[n]\_RXCTL Register Diagram

![Image](31_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_(EMAC)_artifacts/image_000066_51702f622f73bd8b1e640306579d05f3031fa7eaccfc5d5df53b5190cbbf7fca.png)

Table 28-122: EMAC\_DMA[n]\_RXCTL Register Fields

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
|--------------------|------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 31 (R/W)           | RPF        | Rx Packet Flush. The EMAC_DMA[n]_RXCTL.RPF bit enables the Rx packet flush feature. When set (= 1), the EMAC module automatically flushes the packet from the Rx queues designated to this DMARx channel, when it is stopped. When the EMAC_DMA[n]_RXCTL.RPF bit remains set and the DMAis restarted by the software driver, the packets residing in the Rx queues that were received when this RxDMA was stopped, are flushed out. The packets that are received by the MAC after the RxDMA is restarted are routed to the RxDMA. The flushing is done on the read side of the Rx queue. When the EMAC_DMA[n]_RXCTL.RPF bit is cleared (= 0), the EMAC module does not flush the packet in the Rx queue destined to this RxDMA channel when it is in STOP state. This operation can cause head-of-line blocking in the corresponding Rx queue. Note: The stopping of packet flow from a Rx DMAchannel to the application by setting RPF works only when there is one-to-one mapping of Rx queue to Rx DMAchannels. In dynamic mapping mode, setting this bit can flush packets from unintended Rx queues which are destined to the stopped Rx DMAchannel. |
| 31 (R/W)           |            | 0 Rx Packet Flush is Disabled                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| 31 (R/W)           |            | 1 Rx Packet Flush is Enabled                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |

Table 28-122: EMAC\_DMA[n]\_RXCTL Register Fields (Continued)

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
|--------------------|------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 21:16 (R/W)        | RXPBL      | Receive Programmable Burst Length. The EMAC_DMA[n]_RXCTL.RXPBL field indicates the maximum number of beats to be transferred in one DMAblock data transfer. The DMAalways attempts max burst as specified in PBL each time it starts a burst transfer on the application bus. Program PBL with any of the following values: 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, or 32. Any other value results in undefined behavior. To transfer more than 32 beats, perform the following steps: 1. Set the 8xPBL mode in the EMAC_DMA[n]_CTL register. 2. Set the RxPBL. Note: The maximum value of RxPBL must be less than or equal to half the Rx queue size (EMAC_RQ[n]_OPMODE.RQS) in terms of beats. This is required so that the Rx queue has space to store at least another Rx PBL worth of data while the RxDMA is transferring a block of data. For example, in the total locations in Rx queue of size 512 bytes is 128, so RxPBL and 8xPBL needs to be programmed to less than or equal to 64. |
| 14:3 (R/W)         | RBSZ_13_Y  | Receive Buffer Size High. RBSZ[13:0] is split into two fields: higher EMAC_DMA[n]_RXCTL.RBSZ_13_Y and lower RBSZ_x_0. The RBSZ[13:0] field indicates the size of the Rx buffers specified in bytes. The maximum buffer size is limited to 16K bytes. The buffer size is applicable to payload buffers when split headers are enabled. Note: The buffer size must be a multiple of 4 bytes. This is required even if the value of buffer address pointer is not aligned to data bus width. Hence, the lower RBSZ_x_0 bits are read-only and the value is considered as all-zero. Thus, the EMAC_DMA[n]_RXCTL.RBSZ_13_Y indicates the buffer size in terms of locations (with the width same as bus width).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| 2:1 (R/NW)         | RBSZ_X_0   | Receive Buffer Size Low. RBSZ[13:0] is split into two fields RBSZ_13_y and RBSZ_x_0. The EMAC_DMA[n]_RXCTL.RBSZ_X_0 field is the lower field whose width is based on data bus width of the configuration. The EMAC_DMA[n]_RXCTL.RBSZ_X_0 field is 2 bits wide. The EMAC_DMA[n]_RXCTL.RBSZ_X_0 field is read-only (RO).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |

## DMA Channel n Extended Receive Control Register

The EMAC\_DMA[n]\_RXCTL2 register controls the Rx features such as Rx descriptor ring length and alternate Rx buffer size.

Figure 28-68: EMAC\_DMA[n]\_RXCTL2 Register Diagram

![Image](31_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_(EMAC)_artifacts/image_000067_8a7e0109fa2e5d845f49ece1d54546fcf67653a185f76bd3ab5da8ef69d4aa11.png)

Table 28-123: EMAC\_DMA[n]\_RXCTL2 Register Fields

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
|--------------------|------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 23:16 (R/W)        | ARBS       | Alternate Receive Buffer Size. The EMAC_DMA[n]_RXCTL2.ARBS field indicates the size in bytes for buffer 1, when programmed to a non-zero value (when the split header feature is not enabled). When the split header feature is enabled, the EMAC_DMA[n]_RXCTL2.ARBS field indicates the buffer size for header data. The maximum alternate buffer is limited to 1020 bytes for the 32-bit data bus width. When EMAC_DMA[n]_RXCTL2.ARBS = 0, the Rx Buffer1 and Rx Buffer2 sizes are based on EMAC_DMA[n]_RXCTL.RBSZ. |
| 9:0 (R/W)          | RDRL       | Receive Descriptor Ring Length. The EMAC_DMA[n]_RXCTL2 register sets the maximum number of Rx descriptors in the circular descriptor ring. The maximum number of descriptors is limited to 1K descriptors. For example, program any value up to 0x3FF in this field. The EMAC_DMA[n]_RXCTL2.RDRL field is 10 bits wide. When programming 0x3FF, there are 1024 descriptors. For 10 descriptors, program it to a value of 0x9.                                                                                         |

## DMA Channel n Receive Interrupt Watchdog Timer Register

The EMAC\_DMA[n]\_RXINTWDTMR register indicates the watchdog timeout for Receive Interrupt (RI) from the DMA. When this register is written with a non-zero value, it enables the watchdog timer for the EMAC\_DMA[n]\_STAT.RI bit.

![Image](31_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_(EMAC)_artifacts/image_000068_bf02220b4665d69476c644eacd2f0f385b4a262998f6ae165dbd21071ba4c497.png)

Units Receive Interrupt Watchdog Timer Count

Figure 28-69: EMAC\_DMA[n]\_RXINTWDTMR Register Diagram

Table 28-124: EMAC\_DMA[n]\_RXINTWDTMR Register Fields

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
|--------------------|------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 17:16 (R/W)        | RWTU       | Receive Interrupt Watchdog Timer Count Units. The EMAC_DMA[n]_RXINTWDTMR.RWTU field indicates the number of SCLK0 cycles corresponding to one unit in the EMAC_DMA[n]_RXINTWDTMR.RWT field. For example, when EMAC_DMA[n]_RXINTWDTMR.RWT =2 and EMAC_DMA[n]_RXINTWDTMR.RWTU = 1, the watchdog timer is configured for 2 * 512 = 1024 SCLK0 cycles. 0 256                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| 7:0 (R/W)          | RWT        | Receive Interrupt Watchdog Timer Count. The EMAC_DMA[n]_RXINTWDTMR.RWT field indicates the number of SCLK0 cy- cles, multiplied by factor indicated in EMAC_DMA[n]_RXINTWDTMR.RWTU field, for which the watchdog timer is set. The watchdog timer is triggered with the programmed value after the RxDMA completes the transfer of a packet for which EMAC_DMA[n]_STAT.RI = 0 regis- ter, because of the setting of Interrupt Enable bit in the corresponding descriptor RDES3[30]. When the watchdog timer runs out, the RI bit is set and the timer is stopped. The watchdog timer is reset when the RI bit is set (=1) because of automatic setting of RI as per the Interrupt Enable bit RDES3[30] of any received packet. |

The EMAC\_DMA[n]\_SFN\_CTLSTAT register contains the control bits for slot function and the status for transmit path.

The default/reset value is 0x07C which corresponds to a slot interval of 125 us.                                            |

The EMAC_DMA[n]_SFN_CTLSTAT.ASC bit is applicable only when the ESC bit is set. Disabled |

## DMA Channel n Transmit Descriptor List Address Register

The EMAC\_DMA[n]\_TXDSC\_ADDR register points the DMA to the start of transmit descriptor list. The descriptor lists reside in the physical memory space of the application and must be 32-bit aligned. The DMA internally converts it to bus width aligned address by making the corresponding LSB to low.

Write to the EMAC\_DMA[n]\_TXDSC\_ADDR register only when the Tx DMA has stopped (EMAC\_DMA[n]\_TXCTL.ST = 0). When stopped, this register can be written with a new descriptor list address. When EMAC\_DMA[n]\_TXCTL.ST = 1, the DMA takes the newly-programmed descriptor base address. If this register is not changed when EMAC\_DMA[n]\_TXCTL.ST = 0, the DMA takes the descriptor address where it was stopped earlier.

Figure 28-72: EMAC\_DMA[n]\_TXDSC\_ADDR Register Diagram

![Image](31_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_(EMAC)_artifacts/image_000071_9103ac4319d562c9ac66a1a9973f1656bbf2f81e3f59e7b93f4edc154a59c201.png)

Table 28-127: EMAC\_DMA[n]\_TXDSC\_ADDR Register Fields

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
|--------------------|------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 31:2 (R/W)         | TDESLA     | Start of Transmit List. The EMAC_DMA[n]_TXDSC_ADDR.TDESLA field contains the base address of the first descriptor in the transmit descriptor list. The DMAignores the LSB bits (1:0) and internally takes these bits as all-zero. Therefore, these LSB bits are read-only (RO). |

## DMA Channel n Transmit Descriptor Ring Length Register

The EMAC\_DMA[n]\_TXDSC\_RLEN register contains the length of the transmit descriptor ring.

Figure 28-73: EMAC\_DMA[n]\_TXDSC\_RLEN Register Diagram

![Image](31_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_(EMAC)_artifacts/image_000072_4ff7748f053d5aef6917c63d71c5cc379b7e0c2c8614c9eeb4ebe05710a13355.png)

Table 28-128: EMAC\_DMA[n]\_TXDSC\_RLEN Register Fields

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
|--------------------|------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 9:0 (R/W)          | TDRL       | Transmit Descriptor Ring Length. The EMAC_DMA[n]_TXDSC_RLEN.TDRL field sets the maximum number of Tx descriptors in the circular descriptor ring. The maximum number of descriptors is limited to 1K descriptors. A minimum ring descriptor length of 4 is recommended. For example, program any value up to 0x3FF in this field. The EMAC_DMA[n]_TXDSC_RLEN.TDRL field is 10 bits wide. To program 0x3FF, 1024 descriptors are available. For 10 descriptors, program it to a value of 0x9. |

## DMA Channel n Transmit Descriptor Tail Pointer Register

The EMAC\_DMA[n]\_TXDSC\_TLPTR register points to an offset from the base and indicates the location of the last valid descriptor.

Figure 28-74: EMAC\_DMA[n]\_TXDSC\_TLPTR Register Diagram

![Image](31_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_(EMAC)_artifacts/image_000073_93fc0dd46294e791570de85a721e5b2e88c215b539c145f28104c06d3dc472d9.png)

Table 28-129: EMAC\_DMA[n]\_TXDSC\_TLPTR Register Fields

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
|--------------------|------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 31:2 (R/W)         | TDTP       | Transmit Descriptor Tail Pointer. The EMAC_DMA[n]_TXDSC_TLPTR.TDTP field contains the tail pointer for the Tx descriptor ring. The software writes the tail pointer to add more descriptors to the Tx channel. The hardware tries to transmit all packets referenced by the descriptors between the head and the tail pointer registers. |

| 21:16 (R/W)        | TXPBL      | Transmit Programmable Burst Length. The EMAC_DMA[n]_TXCTL.TXPBL field indicates the maximum number of beats to be transferred in one DMAblock data transfer. The DMAalways attempts max burst as specified in PBL each time it starts a burst transfer on the application bus. Program PBL with any of the following values: 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, or 32. Any other value results in undefined behavior. To transfer more than 32 beats, perform the following steps: 1. Set the 8xPBL mode in EMAC_DMA[n]_CTL register. 2. Set the TxPBL. Note: The maximum value of TxPBL must be less than or equal to half the Tx queue size (EMAC_TQ[n]_OPMODE.TQS) in terms of beats. This is required so that the Tx queue has space to store at least another Tx PBL worth of data while the MTL Tx queue controller is transferring data to MAC. For example, in 64-bit data width configurations the total locations in Tx queue of size 512 bytes is 64, TxPBL and 8xPBL must be programmed to less than or equal to 32. |

## DMA Interrupt Status Register

The application reads the EMAC\_DMA\_ISTAT register during interrupt service routine or polling to determine the interrupt status of DMA channels, MTL queues, and the MAC.

Figure 28-79: EMAC\_DMA\_ISTAT Register Diagram

![Image](31_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_(EMAC)_artifacts/image_000078_ca3b25c4c1daea147d5985bd0cdf42c4d2ea6a37a243f67d7ac5eb847cbdf4e3.png)

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
|--------------------|------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 17 (R/NW)          | MACIS      | Interrupt Status. The EMAC_DMA_ISTAT.MACIS bit indicates an interrupt event in the MAC. To clear the EMAC_DMA_ISTAT.MACIS bit (=0), the software must read the corre- sponding register in the MAC to get the exact cause of the interrupt and clear its source.     | Interrupt Status. The EMAC_DMA_ISTAT.MACIS bit indicates an interrupt event in the MAC. To clear the EMAC_DMA_ISTAT.MACIS bit (=0), the software must read the corre- sponding register in the MAC to get the exact cause of the interrupt and clear its source.     |
| 16 (R/NW)          | MTLIS      | MTL Interrupt Status. The EMAC_DMA_ISTAT.MTLIS bit indicates an interrupt event in the MTL. To clear the EMAC_DMA_ISTAT.MTLIS bit (=0), the software must read the corre- sponding register in the MTL to get the exact cause of the interrupt and clear its source. | MTL Interrupt Status. The EMAC_DMA_ISTAT.MTLIS bit indicates an interrupt event in the MTL. To clear the EMAC_DMA_ISTAT.MTLIS bit (=0), the software must read the corre- sponding register in the MTL to get the exact cause of the interrupt and clear its source. |
|                    |            | 0                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | MTL Interrupt Status Not Detected                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
|                    |            | 1                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | MTL Interrupt Status Detected                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |

## DMA Mode Register

The EMAC\_DMA\_MODE register establishes the bus operating modes for the DMA.

Figure 28-80: EMAC\_DMA\_MODE Register Diagram

![Image](31_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_(EMAC)_artifacts/image_000079_cb2757cd1f1f59fe3e7f25aacd57ee49023786573d89f647b8da4ca41b638087.png)

Table 28-135: EMAC\_DMA\_MODE Register Fields

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
|--------------------|------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 17:16 (R/W)        | INTM       | Interrupt Mode. The EMAC_DMA_MODE.INTM field defines the interrupt mode of the EMAC mod- ule. The behavior of the following outputs change depending on the following settings: - EMAC_DMA[n]_TX (Transmit Per Channel Interrupt) - EMAC_DMA[n]_RX (Receive Per Channel Interrupt) - EMAC_STAT (Common Interrupt) It also changes the behavior of the EMAC_DMA[n]_STAT.RI and EMAC_DMA[n]_STAT.TI bits. - 00: EMAC_DMA[n]_TX/RX are pulse signals for each TX/RX packet transfer com- pletion events (irrespective of whether corresponding interrupts are enabled) for which IOC bits are enabled in descriptor. EMAC_STAT is also asserted when corresponding interrupts are enabled and cleared only when software clears the corresponding RI/TI status bits. - 01: EMAC_DMA[n]_TX/RX are level signals asserted on TX/RX packet transfer completion event when corresponding interrupts are enabled and deasserted when the software clears the corresponding RI/TI status bits. The EMAC_STAT is not asserted for these TX/RX packet transfer completion events. - 10: EMAC_DMA[n]_TX/RX are level signals asserted on TX/RX packet transfer completion event when corresponding interrupts are enabled and deasserted when the software clears the corresponding RI/TI status bits. However, the signal is asserted again if the same event occurred again before it was cleared. The EMAC_STAT is not asserted for these TX/RX packet transfer completion events. - 11: Reserved For more details, see Transfer Complete Interrupt Behavior. 0 See Above Description 1 See Above Description 2 See Above Description |
| 11 (R/W)           | TXPR       | Transmit Priority. When set, the EMAC_DMA_MODE.TXPR bit indicates that the Tx DMAhas higher priority than the Rx DMAduring arbitration for the system-side bus. 0 Transmit Priority is Disabled 1 Transmit Priority is Enabled                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |

|--------------------|------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 8 (R/W)            | DSPW       | Descriptor Posted Write. When the EMAC_DMA_MODE.DSPW bit is cleared (=0), it indicates that the descrip- tor writes are always non-posted. When set (=1), the EMAC_DMA_MODE.DSPW bit indicates that the descriptor is non-posted only when the IOC (Interrupt on Comple- tion) is set in last descriptor. | 0 (R/W)            | SWR        | Software Reset. When the EMAC_DMA_MODE.SWR bit is set, the MAC and the DMAcontrol- ler reset the logic and all internal registers of the DMA, MTL, and MAC. The EMAC_DMA_MODE.SWR bit is automatically cleared after the reset operation is com- plete in all the EMAC clock domains. Before reprogramming any the EMAC register, a value of zero should be read in the EMAC_DMA_MODE.SWR bit. The EMAC_DMA_MODE.SWR bit must be read at least 4 SCLK0 clock cycles after it is written to 1. Note: The reset operation is complete only when all resets in all active clock domains are deasserted. Therefore, it is essential that all PHY inputs clocks (applicable for the selected PHY interface) are present for software reset completion. The time to complete the software reset operation depends on the frequency of the slowest active clock. Access restriction applies. Write 1 to set. Self-cleared. Note: The reset operation is complete only when all resets in all active clock domains are deasserted. ## DMA System Bus Mode Register

The EMAC\_DMA\_SYSBMODE register controls the behavior of the SPB or SCB requester. It mainly controls burst splitting and number of outstanding requests.

Figure 28-81: EMAC\_DMA\_SYSBMODE Register Diagram

![Image](31_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_(EMAC)_artifacts/image_000080_f850b8d714ee0e6d9db120b22bb55e7762bc18ede433403d6b244fb4cbbf3300.png)

Table 28-136: EMAC\_DMA\_SYSBMODE Register Fields

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                     |
|--------------------|------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 27:24 (R/W)        | WR_OSR_LMT | SCB Maximum Write Outstanding Request Limit. This value limits the maximum outstanding request on the SCB write interface. Maximum outstanding requests = EMAC_DMA_SYSBMODE.WR_OSR_LMT + 1  |
| 19:16 (R/W)        | RD_OSR_LMT | SCB Maximum Read Outstanding Request Limit. This value limits the maximum outstanding request on the SCB read interface. Maxi- mum outstanding requests = EMAC_DMA_SYSBMODE.RD_OSR_LMT + 1. |
| 13 (R/W)           | ONEKBBE    | 1 KB Boundary Crossing Enable. The EMAC_DMA_SYSBMODE.ONEKBBE bit indicates whether the burst transfers performed by the SCB requester do not cross a 1 KB or (the default) 4 KB boundary.   |
| 13 (R/W)           | ONEKBBE    | 0 Disable                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| 13 (R/W)           | ONEKBBE    | 1 Enable                                                                                                                                                                                    |

Table 28-136: EMAC\_DMA\_SYSBMODE Register Fields (Continued)

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
|--------------------|------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 12 (R/W)           | AAL        | Address-Aligned Beats. When the EMAC_DMA_SYSBMODE.AAL = 1, the SCB or SPB requester performs address-aligned burst transfers on read and write channels. When the EMAC_DMA_SYSBMODE.AAL = 0, the SCB or SPB requester performs burst transfers on read and write channels without aligning to address boundaries. |
| 3 (R/W)            | BLEN16     | SCB Burst Length 16. When EMAC_DMA_SYSBMODE.BLEN16 = 1 or EMAC_DMA_SYSBMODE.FB = 1, the SCB requester can select a burst length of 16 on the SCB interface. When EMAC_DMA_SYSBMODE.FB = 0, writing to the EMAC_DMA_SYSBMODE.BLEN16 bit has no effect.                                                             |
| 2 (R/W)            | BLEN8      | 1 Enable SCB Burst Length 8. When EMAC_DMA_SYSBMODE.BLEN8 = 1 or EMAC_DMA_SYSBMODE.FB = 1, the SCB requester can select a burst length of 8 on the SCB interface. When EMAC_DMA_SYSBMODE.FB = 0, writing to the EMAC_DMA_SYSBMODE.BLEN8 bit has no effect.                                                        |
| 1 (R/W)            | BLEN4      | SCB Burst Length 4. When EMAC_DMA_SYSBMODE.BLEN4 = 1 or EMAC_DMA_SYSBMODE.FB = 1, the SCB requester can select a burst length of 4 on the SCB interface. When EMAC_DMA_SYSBMODE.FB = 0, writing to the EMAC_DMA_SYSBMODE.BLEN4 bit has no effect. 0 Disable                                                       |

|--------------------|------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 0 (R/W)            | FB         | Fixed Burst Length. The EMAC_DMA_SYSBMODE.FB bit enables a fixed burst length. When EMAC_DMA_SYSBMODE.FB = 1, the SCB requester initiates burst lengths as indicated by the BLEN16, BLEN8, or BLEN4 field -- Burst transfers of length 1. When EMAC_DMA_SYSBMODE.FB = 0, the SCB requester initiates burst transfers that are equal to or less than the maximum allowed burst length programmed in bits[7:4]. | Fixed Burst Length. ## DMA TBS Control 0 Register

The EMAC\_DMA\_TBS\_CTL0 register is used to control the Time Based Scheduling (TBS) attributes.

Figure 28-82: EMAC\_DMA\_TBS\_CTL0 Register Diagram

![Image](31_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_(EMAC)_artifacts/image_000081_5d2eedfbe9f1a4c1131774c8131d366f86050f8673356c8a3e2f6d1899b4afce.png)

Table 28-137: EMAC\_DMA\_TBS\_CTL0 Register Fields

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
|--------------------|------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 31:8 (R/W)         | FTOS       | Fetch Time Offset. The EMAC_DMA_TBS_CTL0.FTOS field indicates the value in units of 256 nano- seconds, that has to be deducted from the launch time to compute the fetch Time. Max value: 999,999,999 ns, additionally should be smaller than CTR-1 value when ESTM mode is enabled since this value is a modulo CTR value.                             |
| 6:4 (R/W)          | FGOS       | Fetch GSN Offset. The EMAC_DMA_TBS_CTL0.FGOS field indicates the number of GSN slots that must be deducted from the Launch GSN to compute the Fetch GSN. Value valid only when EMAC_DMA_TBS_CTL0.FTOV is set.                                                                                                                                           |
| 0 (R/W)            | FTOV       | Fetch Time Offset Valid. When set (=1), the EMAC_DMA_TBS_CTL0.FTOV bit indicates that the EMAC_DMA_TBS_CTL0.FTOS field is valid. When cleared (=0), the EMAC_DMA_TBS_CTL0.FTOV bit indicates that the Fetch Offset is not valid and the DMAengine can fetch the frames from host memory without any time restric- tions. 0 Fetch Time Offset is Invalid |
| 0 (R/W)            | FTOV       | 1 Fetch Time Offset is Valid                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| 0 (R/W)            | FTOV       |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |

(Subtract 1 from the value before programming). For example, if the SCLK0 is 100MHz, this field must be programmed to value 100 - 1 = 99 (which is 0x63). ## Address Resolution Protocol (ARP) Register

The EMAC\_ARP\_ADDR register contains the IPv4 destination address of the MAC.

| 31:0 (R/W)         | ARPPA      | ARP Protocol Address. The EMAC_ARP_ADDR.ARPPA field contains the IPv4 destination address of the MAC. This address is used for perfect match with the protocol address of the target field in the received ARP packet. |

## MAC Address 0 High Register

The EMAC\_ADDR0\_HI register holds the upper 16 bits of the first 6-byte MAC address of the station. The first DA byte that is received on the (G)MII interface corresponds to the LS byte (Bits [7:0]) of the EMAC\_ADDR0\_LO register. For example, if 0x112233445566 is received (0x11 in lane 0 of the first column) on the (G)MII as the destination address, then the MAC Address 0 Register [47:0] is compared with 0x665544332211.

The MAC address registers are configured to be double-synchronized to the (G)MII clock domains. Hence, the synchronization is triggered only when bits[31:24] (in little endian mode) or bits[7:0] (in big endian mode) of the EMAC\_ADDR0\_LO register are written. For proper synchronization updates, the consecutive writes to this register should be performed only after at least four clock cycles in the (G)MII clock domain.

Figure 28-88: EMAC\_ADDR0\_HI Register Diagram

![Image](31_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_(EMAC)_artifacts/image_000087_e2699e272a2e8c9b40ee26bca7d4f5ecb15bb66c62b653fc170bfad129de955f.png)

Table 28-143: EMAC\_ADDR0\_HI Register Fields

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
|--------------------|------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 31 (R/NW)          | AE         | Address Enable. The EMAC_ADDR0_HI.AE bit is always set (=1).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| 23:16 (R/W)        | DCS        | DMAChannel Select. When EMAC_MAC_EXT_CFG.PDC = 0, the EMAC_ADDR0_HI.DCS field con- tains the binary representation of the DMAchannel number to which an Rx packet whose DA matches the MAC Address 0 content is routed. When EMAC_MAC_EXT_CFG.PDC = 1, the EMAC_ADDR0_HI.DCS field con- tains the one-hot representation of one or more DMAchannel numbers to which an Rx packet whose DA matches the MAC Address 0 content is routed. |
| 15:0 (R/W)         | ADDRHI     | MAC address 0[47:32]. The EMAC_ADDR0_HI.ADDRHI field contains the upper 16 bits [47:32] of the first 6-byte MAC address. The MAC uses this field for filtering the received packets and inserting the MAC address in the Transmit Flow Control (Pause) Packets.                                                                                                                                                                        |

## MAC Address n High Register

The EMAC\_ADDR[i]\_HI register holds the upper 16 bits of the second 6-byte MAC address of the station.

If the MAC address registers are configured to be double-synchronized to the (G)MII clock domains, the synchronization is triggered only when Bits[31:24] (in little-endian mode) or bits[7:0] (in big-endian mode) of the EMAC\_ADDR0\_LO register are written. For proper synchronization updates, the consecutive writes to this EMAC\_ADDR0\_LO register should be performed after at least four clock cycles in the destination clock domain.

## Auxiliary Time Stamp Nanoseconds Register

The EMAC\_TM\_AUXTS\_NSEC register, along with EMAC\_TM\_AUXTS\_SEC register, gives the 64-bit time stamp stored as auxiliary snapshot. These two registers form the read port of a 64-bit wide FIFO with a depth of 4, 8, or 16 as selected while configuring the IP .

Multiple snapshots can be stored in this FIFO. Bits[29:25] in EMAC\_TM\_STAT register indicate the fill-level of the FIFO. The top of the FIFO is removed only when the last byte of EMAC\_TM\_AUXTS\_SEC register is read. In the Little Endian mode, this means when bits[31:24] are read and in Big Endian mode, bits[7:0] are read.

| (R/NW)             |            |                                                                                                                                          |

| 23 (R/W)           | GPSLCE     | Giant Packet Size Limit Control Enable. When the EMAC_MAC_CFG.GPSLCE bit is set, the MAC considers the value in EMAC_MAC_EXT_CFG.GPSL to declare a received packet as giant packet. The EMAC_MAC_CFG.GPSLCE field must be programmed to more than 1,518 bytes. Otherwise, the MAC considers 1,518 bytes as giant packet limit. When EMAC_MAC_CFG.GPSLCE = 0, the MAC considers a received packet as giant packet when its size is greater than 1,518 bytes (1522 bytes for tagged packet). The watchdog timeout limit, jumbo packet enable and 2K packet enable have higher precedence over the EMAC_MAC_CFG.GPSLCE bit, that is the MAC considers a received packet as giant packet when its size is greater than 9,018 bytes (9,022 bytes for tagged packet) with jumbo packet enabled and greater than 2,000 bytes with 2K packet enabled. The watchdog timeout, if enabled, terminates the received packet when watchdog limit is reached. The EMAC_MAC_CFG.DM bit is RO with default value of 1'b1 in the full-duplex-only configurations.                                                                                                    |

| 11 (R/W)           | ECRSFD     | Enable Carrier Sense Before Transmission in Full-Duplex Mode. When the EMAC_MAC_CFG.ECRSFD bit is set, the MAC transmitter checks the CRS signal before packet transmission in the full-duplex mode. The MAC starts the transmission only when the CRS signal is low. When EMAC_MAC_CFG.ECRSFD = 0, the MAC transmitter ignores the status of the CRS signal.                                                                                                                                                                          |
| 10 (R/W)           | DO         | Disable Receive Own. When the EMAC_MAC_CFG.DO bit is set, the MAC disables the reception of packets when the gmii_txen_o is asserted in the half-duplex mode. When EMAC_MAC_CFG.DO = 0, the MAC receives all packets given by the PHY. The EMAC_MAC_CFG.DO bit is not applicable in the full-duplex mode.                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| 9 (R/W)            | DCRS       | 1 Disable Receive Own Disable Carrier Sense During Transmission. When the EMAC_MAC_CFG.DCRS bit is set, the MAC transmitter ignores the (G)MII CRS signal during packet transmission in the half-duplex mode. As a result, no errors are generated because of loss of carrier or no carrier during transmission. When EMAC_MAC_CFG.DCRS = 0, the MAC transmitter generates errors because of carrier sense. The MAC can even abort the transmission.                                                                                   |
| 8 (R/W)            | DR         | 0 Enable Carrier Sense During Transmission 1 Disable Carrier Sense During Transmission Disable Retry. When the EMAC_MAC_CFG.DR bit is set, the MAC attempts only one transmission. When a collision occurs on the GMII or MII interface, the MAC ignores the current packet transmission and reports a packet abort error with excessive collision error in the Tx packet status. When EMAC_MAC_CFG.DR = 0, the MAC retries based on the settings of the BL field. The EMAC_MAC_CFG.DR bit is applicable only in the half-duplex mode. |

| 4 (R/W)            | DC         | Deferral Check. When the EMAC_MAC_CFG.DC bit is set, the deferral check function is enabled in the MAC. The MAC issues a packet abort status, along with the excessive deferral error bit set in the Tx packet status, when the Tx state machine is deferred for more than 24,288 bit times in 10 or 100 Mbps mode. If the MAC is configured for 1000 Mbps operation, the threshold for deferral is 155,680 bits times. Deferral begins when the transmitter is ready to transmit, but it is prevented because of an active carrier sense signal (CRS) on GMII or MII. The defer time is not cumulative. For example, if the transmitter defers for 10,000 bit times because the CRS signal is active and the CRS signal becomes inactive, the transmitter transmits and collision happens. Because of collision, the transmitter needs to back off and then defer again after back off completion. In such a scenario, the deferral timer is reset (=0), and it is restarted. When EMAC_MAC_CFG.DC = 0, the deferral check function is disabled and the MAC defers until the CRS signal goes inactive. The EMAC_MAC_CFG.DC bit is applicable only in the half-duplex mode. | Deferral Check. When the EMAC_MAC_CFG.DC bit is set, the deferral check function is enabled in the MAC. The MAC issues a packet abort status, along with the excessive deferral error bit set in the Tx packet status, when the Tx state machine is deferred for more than 24,288 bit times in 10 or 100 Mbps mode. If the MAC is configured for 1000 Mbps operation, the threshold for deferral is 155,680 bits times. Deferral begins when the transmitter is ready to transmit, but it is prevented because of an active carrier sense signal (CRS) on GMII or MII. The defer time is not cumulative. For example, if the transmitter defers for 10,000 bit times because the CRS signal is active and the CRS signal becomes inactive, the transmitter transmits and collision happens. Because of collision, the transmitter needs to back off and then defer again after back off completion. In such a scenario, the deferral timer is reset (=0), and it is restarted. When EMAC_MAC_CFG.DC = 0, the deferral check function is disabled and the MAC defers until the CRS signal goes inactive. The EMAC_MAC_CFG.DC bit is applicable only in the half-duplex mode. |
