## MAC Split Mode and Offset Configuration Register

The EMAC\_SPLM\_OFST\_CFG register contains the split mode control field and offset field for the split header feature.

Figure 28-98: EMAC\_SPLM\_OFST\_CFG Register Diagram

![Image](31_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_(EMAC)_artifacts/image_000097_9059acb10c5e71bb193dd33ceca511aa095fd6b6ff90ce9d6830673bd78f95c3.png)

Table 28-153: EMAC\_SPLM\_OFST\_CFG Register Fields

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
|--------------------|------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 24 (R/W)           | SAVE       | Split AV Enable. When EMAC_SPLM_OFST_CFG.SAVE = 1, and the received packet is an AV Type packet, the header is split at SAVO bytes from the beginning of Length/Type field of the packet, for L2 Split. When EMAC_SPLM_OFST_CFG.SAVE = 0, header is split at SPLOFST bytes from the beginning of Length/Type field of the frame, for L2 Split.                                   |
| 22:16 (R/W)        | SAVO       | Split AV Offset. When SAVE bit is set (=1), and the received packet is an AV Type packet, the EMAC_SPLM_OFST_CFG.SAVO field indicates the value of the offset from the beginning of Length/Type field at which header should be split, when appropriate SPLM is selected. The reset value of this field is 2 bytes, indicating a split at L2 header. Value is in terms of bytes. |

Table 28-153: EMAC\_SPLM\_OFST\_CFG Register Fields (Continued)

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
|--------------------|------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 9:8 (R/W)          | SPLM       | Split Mode. The EMAC_SPLM_OFST_CFG.SPLM field indicates the mode of splitting the in- coming Rx packets.                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| 9:8 (R/W)          | SPLM       | 0 Split at L3/L4 Header                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| 9:8 (R/W)          | SPLM       | 1 Split at L2 Header with an Offset. Always Split at SPLOFST Bytes from the Beginning of Length/Type Field of the Frame                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| 9:8 (R/W)          | SPLM       | 2 Combination Mode: Split Similar to SPLM=00 for IP Packets That are Untagged or Tagged and VLAN Strip- ped                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| 9:8 (R/W)          | SPLM       | 3 Reserved                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| 6:0 (R/W)          | SPLOFST    | Split Offset. The EMAC_SPLM_OFST_CFG.SPLOFST field indicates the value of offset from the beginning of Length/Type field at which header split should take place when the appropriate SPLM is selected. The reset value of this field is 2 bytes indicating a split at L2 header. Value is in terms of bytes. |

## Hash Table Register 0

The EMAC\_HASHTBL\_REG0 register contains the first 32 bits of the hash table.

The hash table is used for group address filtering. For hash filtering, the content of the destination address in the incoming packet is passed through the CRC logic and the upper six bits of 64-bit hash (eight in 256-bit hash) bits of the CRC register are used to index the content of the hash table. The most significant bits determines the register to be used (Hash Table Register n), and the least significant five bits determine the bit within the register. For example, a hash value of 6'b100000 (in 64-bit Hash) selects bit 0 of the Hash Table Register 1, a value of 8b'10111111 (in 256-bit hash) selects bit 31 of the Hash Table Register 5.

The hash value of the destination address is calculated in the following way:

1. Calculate the 32-bit CRC for the DA (See IEEE 802.3, Section 3.2.8 for the steps to calculate CRC32).
2. Perform bitwise reversal for the value obtained in Step 1.
3. Take the upper 6 (or 7 or 8) bits from the value obtained in step 2.

If the corresponding bit value of the register is 1'b1, the packet is accepted. Otherwise, it is rejected. If EMAC\_MACPKT\_FILT.PM = 1, all multicast packets are accepted regardless of the multicast hash values.

The hash table register is configured to be double-synchronized to the (G)MII clock domain; the synchronization is triggered only when bits[31:24] (in little-endian mode) or bits[7:0] (in big-endian mode) of the Hash Table Register n registers are written.

Hence, consecutive writes to this register should be performed only after at least four clock cycles in the (G)MII clock domain.

Figure 28-106: EMAC\_HASHTBL\_REG0 Register Diagram

![Image](31_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_(EMAC)_artifacts/image_000105_36a66aea50277e5addc3bd56d5f8bd226e463339c7a631ff3e8800d8fe7c4b6e.png)

Table 28-161: EMAC\_HASHTBL\_REG0 Register Fields

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                               |
|--------------------|------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 31:0 (R/W)         | HT31T0     | MAC Hash Table First 32 Bits. The EMAC_HASHTBL_REG0.HT31T0 field contains the first 32 bits [31:0] of the hash table. |

## Indirect Access Control Register

The EMAC\_INDR\_ACC\_CTL register provides the indirect access control and status for MAC\_&lt;MSEl&gt;\_&lt;AOFF&gt; registers.

Figure 28-114: EMAC\_INDR\_ACC\_CTL Register Diagram

![Image](31_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_(EMAC)_artifacts/image_000113_40376086dab14b14bfd2e1fe7e72312178a198abfae408ca84c103fab779abaf.png)

Table 28-169: EMAC\_INDR\_ACC\_CTL Register Fields

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
|--------------------|------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 19:16 (R/W)        | MSEL       | Mode Select. The EMAC_INDR_ACC_CTL.MSEL field is used in indirect access of MAC_<MSEL>_<AOFF>. The EMAC_INDR_ACC_CTL.MSEL field must be set along with initiation of read/write to MAC_<MSEL>_<AOFF> and should not be changed until the OB is cleared. Values: - 0000:Typ_RXQ_ (Type based RXQ mapping) - 0001-1111: Reserved                                                                                                             |
| 15:8 (R/W)         | AOFF       | Address Offset. The EMAC_INDR_ACC_CTL.AOFF field is used in indirect access of MAC_<MSEL>_<AOFF>. The EMAC_INDR_ACC_CTL.AOFF field must be con- figured along with initiation of read/write to MAC_<MSEL>_<AOFF> and should not be changed until the OB is cleared. Values: - 00000000: IndReg0(Indirect register 0) - 00000001: IndReg1(Indirect register 1) - ... - 00000111: IndReg7(Indirect register 7) - 00001000-11111111: Reserved |

Table 28-169: EMAC\_INDR\_ACC\_CTL Register Fields (Continued)

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
|--------------------|------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 5 (R/W)            | AUTO       | Auto Increment Enable. The EMAC_INDR_ACC_CTL.AUTO bit enables the address offset auto increment feature. When set (=1), AOFF is incremented by 1. Software should ensure not to cause a wrap condition. Byte wise read/write is not supported when auto increment is enabled. When the EMAC_INDR_ACC_CTL.AUTO bit is cleared (=0), AOFF is not incremented automatically. Software should program the correct Address Offset for each access.                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| 1 (R/W)            | COM        | Command Type. The EMAC_INDR_ACC_CTL.COM bit indicates the register access type. - 1: Indi- cates a read operation. - 0: Indicates a write operation.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| 1 (R/W)            | COM        | 0 Write Operation                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| 1 (R/W)            | COM        | 1 Read Operation                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| 0 (R/W)            | OB         | Operation Busy. The EMAC_INDR_ACC_CTL.OB bit is set along with a read or write com- mand for initiating the indirect access to MAC_<MSEL>_<AOFF> register. The EMAC_INDR_ACC_CTL.OB bit is cleared (=0) when the read or write com- mand to MAC_<MSEL>_<AOFF> register is complete. The next indirect reg- ister access can be initiated only after EMAC_INDR_ACC_CTL.OB = 0. Dur- ing a write operation, the bit is cleared (=0) only after the data has been written into MAC_<MSEL>_<AOFF> register. During a read operation, the data should be read from the EMAC_INDR_ACC_DAT register only after EMAC_INDR_ACC_CTL.OB = 0. |

Table 28-171: EMAC\_INVLAN\_INCL Register Fields (Continued)

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
|--------------------|------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 17:16 (R/W)        | VLC        | VLAN Tag Control in Transmit Packets. The EMAC_INVLAN_INCL.VLC field indicates the VLAN tag control in transmit packets. 2'b00: No VLAN tag deletion, insertion, or replacement 2'b01: VLAN tag deletion. The MAC removes the VLAN type (bytes 17 and 18) and VLAN tag (bytes 19 and 20) of all transmitted packets with VLAN tags. 2'b10: VLAN tag insertion. The MAC inserts VLT in bytes 19 and 20 of the packet after inserting the Type value (0x8100 or 0x88a8) in bytes 17 and 18. This operation is performed on all transmitted packets, irrespective of whether they already have a VLAN tag. 2'b11: VLAN tag replacement. The MAC replaces VLT in bytes 19 and 20 of all VLAN-type transmitted packets (Bytes 17 and 18 are 0x8100 or 0x88a8). Note: Changes to this field take effect only on the start of a packet. If this register field is written to when a packet is being transmitted, only the subsequent packet can use the updated value; the current packet does not use the updated value. 0 No VLAN Tag Deletion, Insertion, or Replacement |
| 15:0 (R/W)         | VLT        | VLAN Tag for Transmit Packets. The EMAC_INVLAN_INCL.VLT field contains the value of the VLAN tag to be inserted or replaced. The value must only be changed when the transmit lines are inactive or during the initialization phase. Bits[15:13] are the User Priority field, Bit 12 is the CFI/DEI field, and bits[11:0] are the VID field in the VLAN tag. The following list describes the bits of this field: - Bits[15:13]: User Priority - Bit 12: Canonical Format Indicator (CFI) or Drop Eligible Indicator (DEI) - Bits[11:0]: VLAN Identifier (VID) field of VLAN tag                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |

## Layer 3 and Layer 4 Control Register

The EMAC\_L3L4\_CTL7 register controls the operations of filter 0 of layer 3 and layer 4.

![Image](31_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_(EMAC)_artifacts/image_000118_e188442aac76dee4f6bc86c38e5f16e7195a163a00d6fd6b2404bc1510a2a892.png)

Layer 4 Destination Port Match Enable

Figure 28-119: EMAC\_L3L4\_CTL7 Register Diagram

Table 28-174: EMAC\_L3L4\_CTL7 Register Fields

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
|--------------------|------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 28 (R/W)           | DMCHEN     | DMAChannel Select Enable. When set, the EMAC_L3L4_CTL7.DMCHEN bit enables the selection of theDMA channel number for the packet that is passed by this L3_L4 filter. The DMAchannel is indicated by the DMCHNbits. When EMAC_L3L4_CTL7.DMCHEN = 0, the DMAchannel is not decided by this filter. 0 DMAChannel Select is Disabled |
| 26:24 (R/W)        | DMCHN      | DMAChannel Number. When DMCHENis set (=1), the EMAC_L3L4_CTL7.DMCHN field selects the DMAchannel number to which the packet passed by this filter is routed. The width of the EMAC_L3L4_CTL7.DMCHN field depends on the number of the DMAchannels present in the configuration.                                                  |

| Bit No. (Access)   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
|--------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 21 (R/W)           | Layer 4 Destination Port Inverse Match Enable. When the EMAC_L3L4_CTL7.L4DPIM bit is set, the Layer 4 Destination Port number field is enabled for inverse matching. When EMAC_L3L4_CTL7.L4DPIM = 0, the Layer 4 Destination Port number field is enabled for perfect matching. The EMAC_L3L4_CTL7.L4DPIM bit is valid and applicable only when the EMAC_L3L4_CTL[n].L4DPM= 1.                              |
| 20 (R/W)           | Layer 4 Destination Port Match Enable. When the EMAC_L3L4_CTL7.L4DPM bit is set, the Layer 4 Destination Port number field is enabled for matching. When EMAC_L3L4_CTL7.L4DPM = 0, the MAC ignores the Layer 4 Destination Port number field for matching.                                                                                                                                                  |
| 19 (R/W)           | 1 Layer 4 Destination Port Match is Enabled Layer 4 Source Port Inverse Match Enable. When the EMAC_L3L4_CTL7.L4SPIM bit is set, the Layer 4 Source Port number field is enabled for inverse matching. When EMAC_L3L4_CTL7.L4SPIM = 0, the Layer 4 Source Port number field is enabled for perfect matching. The EMAC_L3L4_CTL7.L4SPIM bit is valid and applicable only when the EMAC_L3L4_CTL[n].L4SPM= 1. |
| 18 (R/W)           | 1 Layer 4 Source Port Inverse Match is Enabled Layer 4 Source Port Match Enable. When the EMAC_L3L4_CTL7.L4SPM bit is set, the Layer 4 Source Port number field is enabled for matching. When EMAC_L3L4_CTL7.L4SPM = 0, the MAC ignores the Layer 4 Source Port number field for matching.                                                                                                                  |

For IPv4 packets, the EMAC_L3L4_CTL7.L3HDBM field contains the number of higher bits of IP Destination Address that are matched in the IPv4 packets. The following list describes the values of this field: - 0: No bits are masked - 1: LSb[0] is masked - 2: Two LSbs [1:0] are masked - .. - 31: All bits except MSb are masked For IPv6 packets, the bits[12:11] of this field correspond to bits[6:5] of L3HSBM which indicate the number of lower bits of IP Source or Destination Address that are masked in the IPv6 packets. The following list describes the concatenated values of the L3HDBM[1:0] and L3HSBM bits: - 0: No bits are masked - 1: LSb[0] is masked - 2: Two LSbs [1:0] are masked - .. - 127: All bits except MSb are masked The EMAC_L3L4_CTL7.L3HDBM field is valid and applicable only when the L3DAM or L3SAM bit is set. |

| 2 (R/W)            | L3SAM      | Layer 3 IP SA Match Enable. When the EMAC_L3L4_CTL[i].L3SAM bit is set, the Layer 3 IP Source Address field is enabled for matching. When EMAC_L3L4_CTL[i].L3SAM = 0, the MAC ignores the Layer 3 IP Source Address field for matching. Note: When the EMAC_L3L4_CTL[n].L3PEN bit is set, set either the EMAC_L3L4_CTL[i].L3SAM bit or the EMAC_L3L4_CTL[n].L3DAM bit be- cause either IPv6 SA or DA can be checked for filtering. 0 Layer 3 IP SA Match is Disabled |
| 0 (R/W)            | L3PEN      | Layer 3 Protocol Enable. When the EMAC_L3L4_CTL[i].L3PEN bit is set, the Layer 3 IP Source or Destination Address matching is enabled for IPv6 packets. When EMAC_L3L4_CTL[i].L3PEN = 0, the Layer 3 IP Source or Destination Address matching is enabled for IPv4 packets. The layer 3 matching is done only when the EMAC_L3L4_CTL[n].L3SAM or EMAC_L3L4_CTL[n].L3DAM bit is set (=1). 0 Layer 3 Protocol is Disabled                                              |
| 0 (R/W)            | L3PEN      |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| 0 (R/W)            | L3PEN      |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |

## LPI Control and Status Register

The EMAC\_LPI\_CTLSTAT register controls the LPI functions and provides the LPI interrupt status. The status bits are cleared when this register is read.

Figure 28-121: EMAC\_LPI\_CTLSTAT Register Diagram

![Image](31_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_(EMAC)_artifacts/image_000120_a6e5f9d089804983f92079b209469b67dde52c50a46937017058f233f5ebeb0c.png)

Table 28-176: EMAC\_LPI\_CTLSTAT Register Fields

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
|--------------------|------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 20 (R/W)           | LPIATE     | LPI Timer Enable. The EMAC_LPI_CTLSTAT.LPIATE bit controls the automatic entry of the MAC transmitter into and exit out of the LPI state. When LPIATE, LPITXA and LPIEN bits are set, the MAC transmitter enters LPI state only when the complete MAC TX data path is IDLE for a period indicated by the EMAC_LPI_ENTR_TMR register. After entering LPI state, if the data path becomes non-IDLE (due to a new packet being accepted for transmission), the transmitter exits LPI state but does not clear LPIEN bit. This enables the re-entry into LPI state when it is IDLE again. When EMAC_LPI_CTLSTAT.LPIATE = 0, the LPI auto timer is disabled and MAC transmitter enters LPI state based on the settings of LPITXA and LPIEN bit descriptions. 0 LPI Timer is Disabled |
| 20 (R/W)           | LPIATE     | 1 LPI Timer is Enabled                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| 20 (R/W)           | LPIATE     |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |

Table 28-176: EMAC\_LPI\_CTLSTAT Register Fields (Continued)

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
|--------------------|------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 19 (R/W)           | LPITXA     | LPI Tx Automate. The EMAC_LPI_CTLSTAT.LPITXA bit controls the behavior of the MAC when it is entering or coming out of the LPI mode on the transmit side. If the EMAC_LPI_CTLSTAT.LPITXA and LPIEN bits are set (=1), the MAC enters the LPI mode only after all outstanding packets (in the IP) and pending packets (in the application interface) have been transmitted. The MAC comes out of the LPI mode when the application sends any packet for transmission or the application issues a Tx FIFO Flush command. In addition, the MAC automatically clears the LPIEN bit when it exits the LPI state. If Tx FIFO flush is set in EMAC_TQ0_OPMODE.FTQ, when the MAC is in the LPI mode, it exits the LPI mode. When the EMAC_LPI_CTLSTAT.LPITXA bit is 0, the LPIEN bit directly controls behavior of the MAC when it is entering or coming out of the LPI mode. 0 LPI Tx Automate is Disabled |
| 18 (R/W)           | PLSEN      | PHY Link Status Enable. The EMAC_LPI_CTLSTAT.PLSEN bit enables the link status received on the RGMII receive paths to be used for activating the LPI LS TIMER. When the EMAC_LPI_CTLSTAT.PLSEN bit is set, the MAC uses the link-status bits of the EMAC_PHYIF_CTLSTAT register and the PLS bit for the LPI LS timer trigger. When EMAC_LPI_CTLSTAT.PLSEN = 0, the MAC ignores the link-status bits of the EMAC_PHYIF_CTLSTAT register and takes only the PLS bit.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| 17 (R/W)           | PLS        | 1 PHY Link Status is Enabled PHY Link Status. The EMAC_LPI_CTLSTAT.PLS bit indicates the link status of the PHY. The MAC transmitter asserts the LPI pattern only when the link status is up (OKAY) at least for the time indicated by the LPI LS TIMER. When the EMAC_LPI_CTLSTAT.PLS bit is set, the link is considered to be okay (UP) and when EMAC_LPI_CTLSTAT.PLS = 0, the link is considered to be down. 0 Link is Down 1 Link is Okay (UP)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |

Table 28-176: EMAC\_LPI\_CTLSTAT Register Fields (Continued)

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
|--------------------|------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 16 (R/W)           | LPIEN      | LPI Enable. When the EMAC_LPI_CTLSTAT.LPIEN bit is set, it instructs the MAC transmit- ter to enter the LPI state. When EMAC_LPI_CTLSTAT.LPIEN = 0, it instructs the MAC to exit the LPI state and resume normal transmission. The EMAC_LPI_CTLSTAT.LPIEN bit is cleared when the LPITXA bit is set and the MAC exits the LPI state because of the arrival of a new packet for transmission.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| 9 (R/NW)           | RLPIST     | Receive LPI State. When the EMAC_LPI_CTLSTAT.RLPIST bit is set, it indicates that the MAC is receiving the LPI pattern on the GMII or MII interface.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| 8 (R/NW)           | TLPIST     | Transmit LPI State. When the EMAC_LPI_CTLSTAT.TLPIST bit is set, it indicates that the MAC is transmitting the LPI pattern on the GMII or MII interface.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| 3 (R/NW)           | RLPIEX     | Receive LPI Exit. When the EMAC_LPI_CTLSTAT.RLPIEX bit is set, it indicates that the MAC re- ceiver has stopped receiving the LPI pattern on the GMII or MII interface, exited the LPI state, and resumed the normal reception. The EMAC_LPI_CTLSTAT.RLPIEX bit is cleared by a read into this register (or the EMAC_LPI_CTLSTAT.RLPIEX bit is written to 1 when EMAC_CSR_SW_CTL.RCWE = 1). Note: The EMAC_LPI_CTLSTAT.RLPIEX bit might not be set if the MAC stops receiving the LPI pattern for a very short duration, such as, less than three clock cycles of SCLK0. 0 Receive LPI Exit Not Detected 1 Receive LPI Exit Detected |
| 3 (R/NW)           |            |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |

Table 28-176: EMAC\_LPI\_CTLSTAT Register Fields (Continued)

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
|--------------------|------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 2 (R/NW)           | RLPIEN     | Receive LPI Entry. When the EMAC_LPI_CTLSTAT.RLPIEN bit is set, it indicates that the MAC receiver has received an LPI pattern and entered the LPI state. The EMAC_LPI_CTLSTAT.RLPIEN bit is cleared by a read into this reg- ister (or the EMAC_LPI_CTLSTAT.RLPIEN bit is written to 1 when EMAC_CSR_SW_CTL.RCWE = 1). Note: The EMAC_LPI_CTLSTAT.RLPIEN bit might not be set if the MAC stops receiving the LPI pattern for a very short duration, such as, less than three clock cycles of SCLK0. |
| 1 (R/NW)           | TLPIEX     | Transmit LPI Exit. When the EMAC_LPI_CTLSTAT.TLPIEX bit is set, it indicates that the MAC transmitter exited the LPI state after the application cleared the LPIEN bit and the LPI TWtimer has expired. The EMAC_LPI_CTLSTAT.TLPIEX bit is cleared by a read into this register (or the EMAC_LPI_CTLSTAT.TLPIEX bit is written to 1 when EMAC_CSR_SW_CTL.RCWE = 1). 0 Transmit LPI Exit Not Detected                                                                                                 |
| 0 (R/NW)           | TLPIEN     | 1 Transmit LPI Exit Detected Transmit LPI Entry. When the EMAC_LPI_CTLSTAT.TLPIEN bit is set, it indicates that the MAC transmitter has entered the LPI state because of the setting of the LPIEN bit. The EMAC_LPI_CTLSTAT.TLPIEN bit is cleared by a read into this reg- ister (or the EMAC_LPI_CTLSTAT.TLPIEN bit is written to 1 when EMAC_CSR_SW_CTL.RCWE = 1). 0 Transmit LPI Entry Not Detected 1 Transmit LPI Entry Detected                                                                 |

## Transmit LPI Entry Timer Register

The EMAC\_LPI\_ENTR\_TMR register controls the Tx LPI entry timer. This counter is enabled only when EMAC\_LPI\_CTLSTAT.LPITE = 1.

Figure 28-122: EMAC\_LPI\_ENTR\_TMR Register Diagram

![Image](31_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_(EMAC)_artifacts/image_000121_41f46921693f2fb6593352b8e4d579a0ca5219bbd4b67622c8f3c92b0747532d.png)

Table 28-177: EMAC\_LPI\_ENTR\_TMR Register Fields

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
|--------------------|------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 19:3 (R/W)         | LPIET      | LPI Entry Timer. The EMAC_LPI_ENTR_TMR.LPIET field specifies the time in microseconds the MAC waits to enter LPI mode, after it has transmitted all the frames. The EMAC_LPI_ENTR_TMR.LPIET field is valid and used only when LPITE and LPITXA are set (=1). Bits [2:0] are read-only so that the granularity of this timer is in steps of 8 microsec- onds. |

## LPI Timers Control Register

The EMAC\_LPI\_TMRSCTL register controls the timeout values in the LPI states. It specifies the time for which the MAC transmits the LPI pattern and also the time for which the MAC waits before resuming the normal transmission.

Figure 28-123: EMAC\_LPI\_TMRSCTL Register Diagram

![Image](31_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_(EMAC)_artifacts/image_000122_f9b94a002e07bcc26a06b8850b286bdfd1bdde0170ee0dcf25b8728f11f4c495.png)

Table 28-178: EMAC\_LPI\_TMRSCTL Register Fields

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
|--------------------|------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 25:16 (R/W)        | LST        | LPI LS Timer. The EMAC_LPI_TMRSCTL.LST field specifies the minimum time (in milliseconds) for which the link status from the PHY should be up (OKAY) before the LPI pattern can be transmitted to the PHY. The MAC does not transmit the LPI pattern even when the LPIEN bit is set unless the LPI LS Timer reaches the programmed terminal count. The default value of the LPI LS Timer is 1000 (1 sec) as defined in the IEEE standard. |
| 15:0 (R/W)         | TWT        | LPI TWTimer. The EMAC_LPI_TMRSCTL.TWT field specifies the minimum time (in microsec- onds) for which the MAC waits after it stops transmitting the LPI pattern to the PHY and before it resumes the normal transmission. The TLPIEX status bit is set after the expiry of this timer.                                                                                                                                                     |

## Layer 3 Address 0 Register 7

For IPv4 packets, the EMAC\_L3\_ADDR0\_REG7 register contains the 32-bit IP Source Address field. For IPv6 packets, it contains bits[31:0] of the 128-bit IP Source Address or Destination Address field.

Figure 28-124: EMAC\_L3\_ADDR0\_REG7 Register Diagram

![Image](31_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_(EMAC)_artifacts/image_000123_397e022a0e3ca0d74ee7e3ce69d3e41581f1a30bfccad5e0dd2d4d9d67928f72.png)

Table 28-179: EMAC\_L3\_ADDR0\_REG7 Register Fields

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
|--------------------|------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 31:0 (R/W)         | L3A        | Layer 3 Address 0 Field. When EMAC_L3L4_CTL[n].L3PEN and EMAC_L3L4_CTL[n].L3SAM = 1, the EMAC_L3_ADDR0_REG7.L3A field contains the value to be matched with bits[31:0] of the IP Source Address field in the IPv6 packets. When EMAC_L3L4_CTL[n].L3PEN and EMAC_L3L4_CTL[n].L3DAM = 1, the EMAC_L3_ADDR0_REG7.L3A field contains the value to be matched with bits[31:0] of the IP Destination Address field in the IPv6 packets. When EMAC_L3L4_CTL[n].L3PEN = 0 and EMAC_L3L4_CTL[n].L3SAM = 1, the EMAC_L3_ADDR0_REG7.L3A field contains the value to be matched with the IP Source Address field in the IPv4 packets. |

## Layer 4 Address Register [i]

The EMAC\_L4\_ADDR7 register is double synchronized to the Rx clock domain. Thus, for proper synchronization updates, the program should perform consecutive writes to the same layer 3/4 address registers only after at least four clock cycles delay of the (G) MII clock domain.

Figure 28-132: EMAC\_L4\_ADDR7 Register Diagram

![Image](31_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_(EMAC)_artifacts/image_000131_4efe85bf983823a25dbf59defacf564e3ba922bf2eeff175d652aaf85f1bd2ef.png)

|--------------------|------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

When EMAC_L3L4_CTL[n].L4PEN = 0 and EMAC_L3L4_CTL[n].L4DPM =1, this field contains the value to be matched with the TCP Destination Port Number field in the IPv4 or IPv6 packets. When the EMAC_L3L4_CTL[n].L4PEN = 0 and EMAC_L3L4_CTL[n].L4DPM =1, this field contains the value to be matched with the UDP Destination Port Number field in the IPv4 or IPv6 packets.                      |
| 15:0 (R/W)         | L4SP       | Layer 4 Source Port Number Field. When EMAC_L3L4_CTL[n].L4PEN = 0 and EMAC_L3L4_CTL[n].L4SPM =1, the EMAC_L4_ADDR7.L4SP field contains the value to be matched with the TCP Source Port Number field in the IPv4 or IPv6 packets. When the EMAC_L3L4_CTL[n].L4PEN = 1 and EMAC_L3L4_CTL[n].L4SPM =1, the EMAC_L4_ADDR7.L4SP field contains the value to be matched with the UDP Source Port Number field in the IPv4 or IPv6 packets. |

## Layer 4 Address Register [i]

The EMAC\_L4\_ADDR[i] register is double synchronized to the Rx clock domain. Thus, for proper synchronization updates, the program should perform consecutive writes to the same layer 3/4 address registers only after at least four clock cycles delay of the (G) MII clock domain.

Figure 28-133: EMAC\_L4\_ADDR[i] Register Diagram

![Image](31_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_(EMAC)_artifacts/image_000132_4efe85bf983823a25dbf59defacf564e3ba922bf2eeff175d652aaf85f1bd2ef.png)

|--------------------|------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 31:16 (R/W)        | L4DP       | Layer 4 Destination Port Number Field. When EMAC_L3L4_CTL[n].L4PEN = 0 and EMAC_L3L4_CTL[n].L4DPM =1, this field contains the value to be matched with the TCP Destination Port Number field in the IPv4 or IPv6 packets. When the EMAC_L3L4_CTL[n].L4PEN = 0 and EMAC_L3L4_CTL[n].L4DPM =1, this field contains the value to be matched with the UDP Destination Port Number field in the IPv4 or IPv6 packets.                          |
| 15:0 (R/W)         | L4SP       | Layer 4 Source Port Number Field. When EMAC_L3L4_CTL[n].L4PEN = 0 and EMAC_L3L4_CTL[n].L4SPM =1, the EMAC_L4_ADDR[i].L4SP field contains the value to be matched with the TCP Source Port Number field in the IPv4 or IPv6 packets. When the EMAC_L3L4_CTL[n].L4PEN = 1 and EMAC_L3L4_CTL[n].L4SPM =1, the EMAC_L4_ADDR[i].L4SP field contains the value to be matched with the UDP Source Port Number field in the IPv4 or IPv6 packets. |

## MDIO Address Register

The EMAC\_MDIO\_ADDR register controls the management cycles to external PHY through a management interface.

Figure 28-135: EMAC\_MDIO\_ADDR Register Diagram

![Image](31_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_(EMAC)_artifacts/image_000134_7783523001435a897ed98145756ccc13488baf4d2cbff34f71fbe5437db41685.png)

|--------------------|------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 27 (R/W)           | PSE        | Preamble Suppression Enable. When the EMAC_MDIO_ADDR.PSE bit is set, the SMA suppresses the 32-bit preamble and transmits MDIO frames with only 1 preamble bit. When the EMAC_MDIO_ADDR.PSE bit is 0, the MDIO frame always has 32 bits of preamble as defined in the IEEE specifications. |
| 27 (R/W)           | PSE        | 0 Preamble Suppression Disabled                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| 27 (R/W)           | PSE        | 1 Preamble Suppression Enabled                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |

Table 28-190: EMAC\_MDIO\_ADDR Register Fields (Continued)

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
|--------------------|------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 26 (R/W)           | BTB        | Back to Back Transactions. When the EMAC_MDIO_ADDR.BTB bit is set and the NTC has value greater than 0, the MAC informs the completion of a read or write command at the end of frame transfer (before the trailing clocks are transmitted). The software can thus initiate the next command which is executed immediately irrespective of the number trailing clocks generated for the previous frame. When EMAC_MDIO_ADDR.BTB = 0, then the read/write command completion (GB is cleared) only after the trailing clocks are generated. In this mode, it is ensured that the NTC is always generated after each frame. The EMAC_MDIO_ADDR.BTB bit must not be set when NTC=0. 0 Back to Back Transactions Disabled |
| 25:21 (R/W)        | PA         | Physical Layer Address. The EMAC_MDIO_ADDR.PA field indicates which Clause 22 PHY devices (out of 32 devices) the MAC is accessing. The EMAC_MDIO_ADDR.PA field indicates which Clause 45 capable PHYs (out of 32 PHYs) the MAC is accessing.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| 20:16 (R/W)        | RDA        | Register/Device Address. The EMAC_MDIO_ADDR.RDA field selects the PHY register in selected Clause 22 PHY device. These bits select the Device (MMD) in selected Clause 45 capable PHY.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| 14:12 (R/W)        | NTC        | Number of Trailing Clocks. The EMAC_MDIO_ADDR.NTC field controls the number of trailing clock cycles generated on ETHx_MDC (MDC) after the end of transmission of MDIO frame. The valid values can be from 0 to 7. Programming the value to 3'h3 indicates that there are additional three clock cycles on the MDCline after the end of MDIO frame transfer.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |

Hence the software must not write or change any of the fields in EMAC_MDIO_ADDR and EMAC_MDIO_DATA registers as long as this bit is set. ## MDIO Data Register

The EMAC\_MDIO\_DATA register stores the write data to be written to the PHY register located at the address specified in EMAC\_MDIO\_ADDR. The EMAC\_MDIO\_DATA register also stores the read data from the PHY register located at the address specified by MDIO Address register.

Figure 28-136: EMAC\_MDIO\_DATA Register Diagram

![Image](31_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_(EMAC)_artifacts/image_000135_7ce8c80227b4e2d35a7da0e70af5f9369a6c603f201c3662882e8a74a8e45cda.png)

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                          |
|--------------------|------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 31:16 (R/W)        | RA         | Register Address. The EMAC_MDIO_DATA.RA field is valid only when EMAC_MDIO_ADDR.C45E = 1. It contains the register address in the PHY for the intended MDIO frame.                                               |
| 15:0 (R/W)         | GD         | GMII Data. The EMAC_MDIO_DATA.GD field contains the 16-bit data value read from the PHY after a management read operation or the 16-bit data value to be written to the PHY before a management write operation. |

## PPS n Interval Register

The EMAC\_PPS[n]\_INTVL register contains the number of units of sub-second increment value between the rising edges of ETH0\_PTPPPSn signal output.

Figure 28-138: EMAC\_PPS[n]\_INTVL Register Diagram

![Image](31_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_(EMAC)_artifacts/image_000137_04f714f67ce20f211fb6dd9a884683ecad08014133eed7ad47c3a81962cfb501.png)

| 31:0 (R/W)         | PPSINT     | PPS Output Signal Interval. The EMAC_PPS[n]_INTVL.PPSINT field stores the interval between the rising edges of the ETH0_PTPPPSn signal output. The interval is stored in terms of number of units of sub-second increment value. Program one value less than the required interval. For example, if the PTP reference clock is 50 MHz (period of 20 ns), and desired interval between the rising edges of the ETH0_PTPPPSn signal output is 100 ns (that is, 5 units of sub-second increment value), program value 4 (5-1) in this register. |

## PPS n Target Time Seconds Register

The EMAC\_PPS[n]\_TGTM\_SEC register, along with the EMAC\_PPS[n]\_TGTM\_NSEC register, is used to schedule an interrupt event (bit 1 of EMAC\_TM\_STAT) when the system time exceeds the value programmed in these registers.

Figure 28-140: EMAC\_PPS[n]\_TGTM\_SEC Register Diagram

![Image](31_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_(EMAC)_artifacts/image_000139_de7f25ba322bd7e83ed700ce30fa11d521b24ad834ae16c3ec10f871a071ceeb.png)

Table 28-195: EMAC\_PPS[n]\_TGTM\_SEC Register Fields

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
|--------------------|------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 31:0 (R/W)         | TSTRH      | PPS Target Time Seconds Register. The EMAC_PPS[n]_TGTM_SEC.TSTRH field stores the time in seconds. When the time stamp value matches or exceeds both target time stamp registers, the MAC starts or stops the PPS signal output and generates an interrupt (if enabled) based on the target time mode selected for the corresponding PPS output in the EMAC_PPS_CTL register. If EMAC_TM_CTL.PTGE = 1 with the presentation time control set in recovery mode, then these bits indicate the TPT being programmed by the application and in generation mode it indicates the CPT generated at the sampled trigger. |

## PPS n Width Register

The EMAC\_PPS[n]\_WID register contains the number of units of sub-second increment value between the rising and corresponding falling edges of ETH0\_PTPPPSn signal output.

Figure 28-141: EMAC\_PPS[n]\_WID Register Diagram

![Image](31_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_(EMAC)_artifacts/image_000140_c58b8a8b4184621781ef59bb89ffafd007110d157083b913a33b3059292d1c5a.png)

Table 28-196: EMAC\_PPS[n]\_WID Register Fields

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
|--------------------|------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 31:0 (R/W)         | PPSWIDTH   | PPS Output Signal Width. The EMAC_PPS[n]_WID.PPSWIDTH field store the width between the rising edge and corresponding falling edge of PPS signal output. The width is stored in terms of number of units of sub-second increment value. Program one value less than the required interval. For example, if PTP reference clock is 50 MHz (period of 20 ns), and width between the rising and corresponding falling edges of PPS signal output is 80 ns (that is, four units of sub-second increment value), program value 3 (4-1) in this register. Note: The value programmed in this register must be lesser than the value program- med in the EMAC_PPS[n]_INTVL register. |

## PPS Control Register

Bits[30:24] of the EMAC\_PPS\_CTL register are valid only when four flexible PPS outputs are selected. Bits[22:16] are valid only when three or more flexible PPS outputs are selected. Bits[14:8] are valid only when two or more flexible PPS outputs are selected. Bits[6:4] are valid only when flexible PPS feature is selected.

| 3:0 (R/W)          | PPSCTRL_PPSCMD | PPS Output Frequency Control. The EMAC_PPS_CTL.PPSCTRL_PPSCMD field controls the frequency of the ETH0_PTPPPS0 output (PTP clock) signal. The default value is 0000, and the PPS output is 1 pulse (of width PTP clock) every second. For other values of EMAC_PPS_CTL.PPSCTRL_PPSCMD , the PPS output becomes a generated clock of following frequencies: - 0001: The binary rollover is 2 Hz, and the digital rollover is 1 Hz. - 0010: The binary rollover is 4 Hz, and the digital rollover is 2 Hz. - 0011: The binary rollover is 8 Hz; digital rollover is 4 Hz. - 0100: The binary rollover is 16 Hz; digital rollover is 8 Hz. ... - 1111: The binary rollover is 32.768 KHz; digital rollover is 16.384 KHz. See the Fixed Pulse-Per-Second Output topic for details. When EMAC_PPS_CTL.PPSCTRL_PPSCMD = 0011, the PPS (4 Hz) is a sequence of: Three clocks of 50 percent duty cycle and 268 ms period. A fourth clock of 195 ms period (134 ms low and 61 ms high). This behavior is due to the non-linear toggling of bits in the digital rollover mode in the EMAC_TM_NSEC register. For Flexible PPS Output (ETH0_PTPPPS0) control, programming the EMAC_PPS_CTL.PPSCTRL_PPSCMD bits with a non-zero value instructs the MAC to initiate an event. When the command is transferred or synchronized to the PTP clock domain, the bits are cleared automatically. Software should ensure that these bits are programmed only when they are 'all-zero'. When EMAC_PPS_CTL.MCGREN0 = 1, the EMAC_PPS_CTL.PPSCTRL_PPSCMD bits are treated as presentation time control bits: - 0000: MCGR operation is not carried out. If configured to this value in the middle of clock recovery or generation, all processing inputs are flushed. - 0001: Capture the presentation time at the rising edge of the EMAC0_MCG_PST trigger request into the EMAC_PPS[0]_TGTM_SEC register. - 0010: Capture the presentation time at the falling edge of the EMAC0_MCG_PST trigger request into the EMAC_PPS[0]_TGTM_SEC register. - 0011: Capture the presentation time at both edges of the EMAC0_MCG_PST trigger request into the EMAC_PPS[0]_TGTM_SEC register. - 0100-1000: Reserved - 1001: Toggle output on compare - 1010: Pulse output low on compare for one PTP clock cycle. - 1011: Pulse output high on compare for one PTP clock cycle. - 1100-1111: Reserved |

## MAC Packet Filter Register

The EMAC\_MACPKT\_FILT register contains the filter controls for receiving packets. Some of the controls from this register go to the address check block of the MAC which performs the first level of address filtering. The second level of filtering is performed on the incoming packet based on other controls such as Pass Bad Packets and Pass Control Packets.

Figure 28-144: EMAC\_MACPKT\_FILT Register Diagram

![Image](31_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_(EMAC)_artifacts/image_000143_8c9372e315c8bf03e5cde5f85dfd470ff2a3a2df16eaaaae84c1adbbdadc47b4.png)

|--------------------|------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 31 (R/W)           | RA         | Receive All. When the EMAC_MACPKT_FILT.RA bit is set, the MAC receiver module passes all received packets to the application, irrespective of whether they pass the address filter or not. The result of the SA or DA filtering is updated (pass or fail) in the corresponding bit in the Rx status word. When EMAC_MACPKT_FILT.RA = 0, the receiver module passes only those packets to the application that pass the SA or DA address filter. 0 Receive All is Disabled |
| 31 (R/W)           | RA         | 1 Receive All is Enabled                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |

## Presentation Time Update Register

The EMAC\_PRSNTM\_UPDT register holds the 32-bit value of MAC 1722 Presentation Time in ns, that should be added to the Current Presentation Time Counter value. Init happens when EMAC\_TM\_CTL.TSINIT = 1, and update happens when EMAC\_TM\_CTL.TSUPDT = 1.

The EMAC\_PRSNTM\_UPDT register exists when DWC\_EQOS\_FLEXI\_PPS\_OUT\_EN is configured.

Figure 28-145: EMAC\_PRSNTM\_UPDT Register Diagram

![Image](31_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_(EMAC)_artifacts/image_000144_1856bd288145a905ff53e5fc4cb2e55a797005af8576df1197d614a73b2079ee.png)

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
|--------------------|------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 31:0 (R/W)         | MPTU       | 1722 Presentation Time Update. The EMAC_PRSNTM_UPDT.MPTU field holds the init value or the update value for the presentation time. When used for update, this field holds the 32-bit value in ns, that should be added to the Current Presentation Time Counter value. When EMAC_TM_NSECUPDT.ADDSUB = 1, this value is directly used for subtraction. |

## Queue 0 Transmit Flow Control Register

The EMAC\_Q0\_TXFLOW\_CTL register controls the generation and reception of the Control (Pause Command) packets by the flow control module of the MAC. A write to a register with the Busy bit set (=1) triggers the Flow Control block to generate a Pause packet. The fields of the control packet are selected as specified in the 802.3x specification, and the Pause Time value from this register is used in the Pause Time field of the control packet. The Busy bit remains set until the control packet is transferred onto the cable. The application must make sure that the Busy bit is cleared before writing to the register.

When the PFCE bit in the MAC\_Rx\_Flow\_Ctrl register is enabled, this register controls the generation of Priority Flow Control (PFC) frames with priorities mapped according to PSRQ0 in the MAC\_RxQ\_Ctrl2 register.

The EMAC_Q0_TXFLOW_CTL.FCB_BPA bit initiates a Pause packet in the full-du- plex mode and activates the backpressure function in the half-duplex mode if the TFE bit is set. In full-duplex mode, the EMAC_Q0_TXFLOW_CTL.FCB_BPA bit should be read as 1'b0 before writing to this register. To initiate a Pause packet, the application must set the EMAC_Q0_TXFLOW_CTL.FCB_BPA bit to 1'b1. During Control packet transfer, the EMAC_Q0_TXFLOW_CTL.FCB_BPA bit continues to be set to indicate that a packet transmission is in progress. When Pause packet transmission is complete, the MAC resets the EMAC_Q0_TXFLOW_CTL.FCB_BPA bit to 1'b0. Do not write to this register until the EMAC_Q0_TXFLOW_CTL.FCB_BPA bit is cleared. When the EMAC_Q0_TXFLOW_CTL.FCB_BPA bit is set (and TFE bit is set) in the half-duplex mode, the MAC asserts the back pressure. During back pressure, when the MAC receives a new packet, the transmitter starts sending a JAM pattern resulting in a collision. This control register bit is logically OR'ed with the mti_flowctrl_i input signal for the back pressure function. When the MAC is configured for the full-duplex mode, the BPA is automatically disabled. Access restriction applies. Write 1 to set. Self-cleared. ## Queue [i] Transmit Flow Control Register

The EMAC\_Q[i]\_TXFLOW\_CTL register controls the generation and reception of the Control (Pause Command) packets by the Flow control module of the MAC. A write to a register with the Busy bit set (= 1) triggers the Flow Control block to generate a Pause packet. The fields of the control packet are selected as specified in the 802.3x specification, and the Pause Time value from this register is used in the Pause Time field of the control packet. The Busy bit remains set until the control packet is transferred onto the cable. The application must make sure that the Busy bit is cleared before writing to the register. (EMAC\_RXFLOW\_CTL.PFCE = 1.)

The register controls the generation of PFC control packets of priorities mapped per the PSRQn field in the EMAC\_RXQ\_CTL2.EMAC\_RXQ\_CTL3 registers.

Figure 28-148: EMAC\_Q[i]\_TXFLOW\_CTL Register Diagram

![Image](31_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_(EMAC)_artifacts/image_000147_584b5e2c3ae6c9ac16411a045389deabca9bdf1de90b476d2d0624ac8035324f.png)

|--------------------|------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 31:16 (R/W)        | PT         | Pause Time. The EMAC_Q[i]_TXFLOW_CTL.PT field holds the value to be used in the Pause Time field in the Tx control packet. The bits are configured to be double-synchronized to the (G)MII clock domain. Hence, consecutive writes to this register should be performed only after at least four clock cycles in the (G)MII clock domain.  |
| 7 (R/W)            | DZPQ       | Disable Zero-Quanta Pause. When the EMAC_Q[i]_TXFLOW_CTL.DZPQ bit is set, it disables the automatic generation of the zero-quanta Pause packets on deassertion of the flow-control signal from the FIFO layer. When EMAC_Q[i]_TXFLOW_CTL.DZPQ = 0, normal operation with automatic zero-quanta Pause packet generation is enabled. Enabled |
| 7 (R/W)            | DZPQ       | 0 Zero-Quanta Pause Packet Generation is                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| 7 (R/W)            | DZPQ       | 1 Zero-Quanta Pause Packet Generation is Disabled                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |

The EMAC_Q[i]_TXFLOW_CTL.PLT field configures the threshold of the Pause timer at which the input flow control signal mti_flowctrl_i is checked for automatic retransmission of the Pause packet. The threshold values must be less than the Pause Time (PT) configured in bits[31:16]. ## Receive Queue Control 1 Register

The EMAC\_RXQ\_CTL1 register controls the routing of multicast, broadcast, AV, DCB, and untagged packets to the Rx queues.

Figure 28-150: EMAC\_RXQ\_CTL1 Register Diagram

![Image](31_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_(EMAC)_artifacts/image_000149_e0e93b6eb6f9dfb765d6ffee14b1a6a5c2ac8ff179773a31b04177aa6f58e801.png)

When the EMAC_RXQ_CTL1.TBRQE bit is set, it enables the Type field based Rx queuing where the Type field of received packet is compared with programmed TYP field in MAC_TMRQ_Regs(n) and if a match occurs the packet is routed to the corresponding TMRQ field.                                                               |
| 28 (R/W)           | OMCBCQ     | Over-riding MC-BC Queue Priority Select. When set (=1), the EMAC_RXQ_CTL1.OMCBCQ bit indicates that the pri- ority of MCBCQ is reduced and the received packet is first routed to PTPQ, AVCPQ, DCBCPQ depending on packet type. When cleared (=0), the EMAC_RXQ_CTL1.OMCBCQ bit indicates that the received multicast/broadcast packet is routed to MCBCQ. Disabled |
