## Receive Queue Control 2 Register

The EMAC\_RXQ\_CTL2 register controls the routing of tagged packets based on the USP (user priority) field of the received packets to the Rx queues 0 to 3.

Figure 28-151: EMAC\_RXQ\_CTL2 Register Diagram

![Image](31_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_(EMAC)_artifacts/image_000150_b330ca15276c61495b84f439eb8cb1871b60cf8159e79cf1d1cb78d31e93c47e.png)

Table 28-206: EMAC\_RXQ\_CTL2 Register Fields

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
|--------------------|------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 31:24 (R/W)        | PSRQ3      | Priorities Selected in the Receive Queue 3. The EMAC_RXQ_CTL2.PSRQ3 field selects the priorities assigned to Rx queue 3. All packets with priorities that match the values set in this field are routed to Rx queue 3. For example, if PSRQ3[6, 3] are set, packets with USP field equal to 3 or 6 are routed to Rx queue 3. The software must ensure that the content of this field is mutually exclusive to the PSRQ fields for other queues, that is, the same priority is not mapped to multiple Rx queues. This field also determines the priorities to be included in the PFC packet sent to remote station when Rx queue 3 crosses the flow control threshold settings. |
| 23:16 (R/W)        | PSRQ2      | Priorities Selected in the Receive Queue 2. The EMAC_RXQ_CTL2.PSRQ2 field selects the priorities assigned to Rx queue 2. All packets with priorities that match the values set in this field are routed to Rx queue 2. For example, if PSRQ2[1, 0] are set, packets with USP field equal to 1 or 0 are routed to Rx queue 2. The software must ensure that the content of this field is mutually exclusive to the PSRQ fields for other queues, that is, the same priority is not mapped to multiple Rx queues. This field also determines the priorities to be included in the PFC packet sent to remote station when Rx queue 2 crosses the flow control threshold settings. |

All packets with priorities that match the values set in this field are routed to Rx queue 1. For example, if PSRQ1[4] is set, packets with USP field equal to 4 are routed to Rx queue 1. The EMAC\_RXQ\_CTL4 register controls the routing of unicast and multicast packets that fail the destination or source address filter to the Rx queues.

Figure 28-153: EMAC\_RXQ\_CTL4 Register Diagram

![Image](31_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_(EMAC)_artifacts/image_000152_beab0ab4d2dfbe0deb6b4033b874b81e7951f07eb1aa3ef00b4be32c17238ff4.png)

When the EMAC_RXQ_CTL4.UDC bit is set along with PDC bit of the MAC_Ext_Configuration register, the MAC provides DMAChannel number speci- fied as one-hot value in DCS field of MAC_Address(#i)_High register that matched the Unicast Destination Address of the received packet. Note: When the above condition is satisfied for unicast packet but the highest Receive Queue selected in configuration is not enabled or when DA/SA/VLAN filter fails and corresponding filter fail Receive Queue is enabled, it is routed to Receive Queue determined by other queuing methods. When the EMAC_RXQ_CTL4.UDC bit is reset, the MAC routes the received pack- et with Unicast Destination Address based on other queuing methods, theDMA Channel number selected is binary value from DCS field of MAC_Address(#i)_High register (if PDC bit is reset) or lowest bit set in one-hot value (if PDC is set) in DCS field of MAC_Address(#i)_High register that matched the Unicast Destination Address of the received packet. |

## MAC Receive Time Domain Increment Register

The EMAC\_MAC\_RX\_DOMAIN\_TIME\_INCR register indicates the increment value of the PTP time maintained in receive clock domain that is used for time stamping.

Figure 28-154: EMAC\_MAC\_RX\_DOMAIN\_TIME\_INCR Register Diagram

![Image](31_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_(EMAC)_artifacts/image_000153_9be06e27863351251af9b0c90bbe8b78274480f147c1c51f2ececb7f995025c5.png)

Table 28-209: EMAC\_MAC\_RX\_DOMAIN\_TIME\_INCR Register Fields

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
|--------------------|------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 31:16 (R/W)        | RXNS       | Receive Domain Time Increment Value in Nanoseconds. The EMAC_MAC_RX_DOMAIN_TIME_INCR.RXNS bit field indicates the nano- second part of the increment value of the PTP time maintained in receive clock domain that is used for time stamping. For example, when operating in 2.5G speed the clock period is 3.2ns, so for digi- tal rollover mode the RXNS and RXSNS fields must be programmed with 3 and (0.2*256)=51 respectively. In binary rollover mode, 3/0.466=6.44 and 0.2+0.44=0.64, so RXNS and RXSNS fields must be programmed with 6 and (0.64*256)=164 respec- tively. When both RXSNS and RXNS fields are all-zeros, the fixed value based on operating speed is used for PTP time increment in receive clock domain. |
| 15:8 (R/W)         | RXSNS      | Receive Domain Time Increment Value in Sub-Nanoseconds. The EMAC_MAC_RX_DOMAIN_TIME_INCR.RXSNS bit field indicates the sub- nanosecond part of the increment value of the PTP time maintained in receive clock domain that is used for time stamping. This field has granularity of 1/256 ns. When both RXSNS and RXNS fields are all-zeros, the fixed value based on operating speed is used for PTP time increment in receive clock domain.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |

## Receive Transmit Status Register

The EMAC\_RXTX\_STAT register contains the receive and transmit error status.

Figure 28-156: EMAC\_RXTX\_STAT Register Diagram

![Image](31_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_(EMAC)_artifacts/image_000155_e6b8a9a0be089c3fc8f5c74b5198b8d2ba818f568df4858754395cf150dcf35d.png)

|--------------------|------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 8 (R/NW)           | RWT        | Receive Watchdog Timeout. The EMAC_RXTX_STAT.RWT bit is set when a packet with length greater than 2,048 bytes is received (10, 240 bytes when jumbo packet mode is enabled (EMAC_MAC_CFG.JE = 1) and EMAC_MAC_CFG.WD = 0. ## Subsecond Increment Register

The EMAC\_TM\_SUBSEC register specifies the value to be added to the internal system time register every cycle of PTP clock.

Figure 28-160: EMAC\_TM\_SUBSEC Register Diagram

![Image](31_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_(EMAC)_artifacts/image_000159_62f0c98949ba58426161d54ccdc60247c50158a43b7eb5d693e77cb5e7ef43c5.png)

Table 28-215: EMAC\_TM\_SUBSEC Register Fields

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
|--------------------|------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 23:16 (R/W)        | SSINC      | Sub-second Increment Value. The value programmed in the EMAC_TM_SUBSEC.SSINC field is accumulated every PTP clock cycle with the contents of the sub-second register. For example, when the PTP clock is 50 MHz (period is 20 ns), program 20 (0x14) when the EMAC_TM_NSEC register has an accuracy of 1 ns (EMAC_TM_CTL.TSCTRLSSR = 1). When EMAC_TM_CTL.TSCTRLSSR = 0, the EMAC_TM_NSEC register has a resolution of ~0.465 ns. In this case, program a value of 43 (0x2B) which is derived by 20 ns/0.465. |
| 15:8 (R/W)         | SNSINC     | Sub-nanosecond Increment Value. The EMAC_TM_SUBSEC.SNSINC field contains the sub-nanosecond increment value, represented in nanoseconds multiplied by 2 8 . This value is accumulated with the sub-nanoseconds field of the subsecond register. For example, when EMAC_TM_CTL.TSCTRLSSR = 1. and if the required increment is 5.3ns, then EMAC_TM_SUBSEC.SSINC should be 0x05 and EMAC_TM_SUBSEC.SNSINC should be 0x4C.                                                                                       |

## System Time Nanoseconds Register

The EMAC\_TM\_NSEC register, along with System Time Seconds register, indicates the current value of the system time maintained by the MAC.

Figure 28-162: EMAC\_TM\_NSEC Register Diagram

![Image](31_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_(EMAC)_artifacts/image_000161_3858dc89c8abd08a9e4928a88b64835bd4ff1033f82b6256863d9ad24036ae99.png)

|--------------------|------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

## System Time Nanoseconds Update Register

MAC System Time Nanoseconds Update register.

Figure 28-163: EMAC\_TM\_NSECUPDT Register Diagram

![Image](31_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_(EMAC)_artifacts/image_000162_9684498e1a634865c0a67a17b735f642cd2d9e38a801e49ae6dcaa4d651ff3c5.png)

Table 28-218: EMAC\_TM\_NSECUPDT Register Fields

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
|--------------------|------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 31 (R/W)           | ADDSUB     | Add or Subtract Time. When the EMAC_TM_NSECUPDT.ADDSUB bit is set, the time value is subtracted with the contents of the update register. When EMAC_TM_NSECUPDT.ADDSUB = 0, the time value is added with the contents of the update register. |
| 31 (R/W)           | ADDSUB     | 0 Add Time                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| 31 (R/W)           | ADDSUB     | 1 Subtract Time                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |

Table 28-218: EMAC\_TM\_NSECUPDT Register Fields (Continued)

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
|--------------------|------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 30:0 (R/W)         | TSSS       | Time Stamp Sub Seconds. The EMAC_TM_NSECUPDT.TSSS field is the sub-seconds part of the update. When EMAC_TM_NSECUPDT.ADDSUB = 1, the EMAC_TM_NSECUPDT.TSSS field must be programmed with the complement of the sub-seconds part of the update value as described. When EMAC_TM_NSECUPDT.ADDSUB = 0, the EMAC_TM_NSECUPDT.TSSS field must be programmed with the sub-seconds part of the update value, with an accuracy based on the EMAC_TM_CTL.TSCTRLSSR bit. For EMAC_TM_CTL.TSCTRLSSR = 1: -- The programmed value must be 10 9 - <sub-second value>. -- Each bit represents 1 ns and the programmed value should not exceed 0x3B9A_C9FF. For EMAC_TM_CTL.TSCTRLSSR = 0: -- The programmed value must be 2 31 - <sub-second_value>. -- Each bit represents an accuracy of 0.46 ns. For example, to subtract 2.000000001 seconds from the system time, then the EMAC_TM_NSECUPDT.TSSS field must be 0x7FFF_FFFF (that is, 2 31 - 1), when EMAC_TM_CTL.TSCTRLSSR = 0 and 0x3B9A_C9FF (that is, 10 9 - 1), when EMAC_TM_CTL.TSCTRLSSR = 1. |

## System Time Seconds Register

The EMAC\_TM\_SEC register, along with the EMAC\_TM\_NSEC register, indicates the current value of the system time maintained by the MAC. Though it is updated on a continuous basis, there is some delay from the actual time because of clock domain transfer latencies (from PTP clock to SCLK0).

Figure 28-164: EMAC\_TM\_SEC Register Diagram

![Image](31_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_(EMAC)_artifacts/image_000163_8439177b4f588b910a128ffd81a16eeb5bb3a1cbee1f8f0cfb156eb9883800cc.png)

Table 28-219: EMAC\_TM\_SEC Register Fields

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                    |
|--------------------|------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 31:0 (R/NW)        | TSS        | Time Stamp Second. The value in the EMAC_TM_SEC.TSS field indicates the current value in seconds of the System Time maintained by the MAC. |

## System Time Seconds Update Register

The EMAC\_TM\_SECUPDT register, along with the EMAC\_TM\_NSECUPDT register, initializes or updates the system time maintained by the MAC. Write both registers before setting the EMAC\_TM\_CTL.TSINIT or EMAC\_TM\_CTL.TSUPDT bits.

Figure 28-165: EMAC\_TM\_SECUPDT Register Diagram

![Image](31_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_(EMAC)_artifacts/image_000164_54ce68309e2ebe4b74a4b5c4ea22c56caf8560cd7c31604e5ee710d4d7f8888e.png)

Table 28-220: EMAC\_TM\_SECUPDT Register Fields

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
|--------------------|------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 31:0 (R/W)         | TSS        | Time Stamp Seconds. The value in the EMAC_TM_SECUPDT.TSS field is the seconds part of the update. When EMAC_TM_NSECUPDT.ADDSUB = 0, the EMAC_TM_SECUPDT.TSS field must be programmed with the seconds part of the update value. When EMAC_TM_NSECUPDT.ADDSUB = 1, the EMAC_TM_SECUPDT.TSS field must be programmed with the complement of the seconds part of the update value. For example, to subtract 2.000000001 seconds from the system time, the EMAC_TM_SECUPDT.TSS field must be 0xFFFF_FFFE (that is, 2 32 - 2). |

## Time Stamp Addend Register

The EMAC\_TM\_ADDEND register value is used only when the system time is configured for Fine Update mode (EMAC\_TM\_CTL.TSCFUPDT). The content of this register is added to a 32-bit accumulator in every clock cycle (PTP clock) and the system time is updated when the accumulator overflows.

Figure 28-166: EMAC\_TM\_ADDEND Register Diagram

![Image](31_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_(EMAC)_artifacts/image_000165_8c78f2f49dffa994cd4153c7cba81ff6f6ab031aa0ecd0532a578b8539e42e74.png)

Table 28-221: EMAC\_TM\_ADDEND Register Fields

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                           |
|--------------------|------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 31:0 (R/W)         | TSAR       | Timestamp Addend Register. The EMAC_TM_ADDEND.TSAR field indicates the 32-bit time value to be added to the Accumulator register to achieve time synchronization. |

## Time Stamp Control Register

The EMAC\_TM\_CTL register controls the operation of the System Time generator and processing of PTP packets for time stamping in the receiver.

Figure 28-167: EMAC\_TM\_CTL Register Diagram

![Image](31_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_(EMAC)_artifacts/image_000166_c7515367df14f7fabba563577d8fb043361a4b2ba079e4aa5331a4e03638fd59.png)

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name    | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
|--------------------|-------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 28 (R/W)           | AV8021ASMEN | AV 802.1AS Mode Enable. When the EMAC_TM_CTL.AV8021ASMEN bit is set, the MAC processes only untagged PTP over Ethernet packets for providing PTP status and capturing time stamp snapshots, that is, IEEE 802.1AS mode of operation. When PTP offload feature is enabled, for the purpose of PTP offload, the transport specific field in the PTP header is generated and checked based on the value of the EMAC_TM_CTL.AV8021ASMEN bit. 0 AV 802.1AS Mode is Disabled                                                        |
| 24 (R/W)           | TXTSSTSM    | Transmit Time Stamp Status Mode. When the EMAC_TM_CTL.TXTSSTSM bit is set, the MAC overwrites the earlier transmit time stamp status even if it is not read by the software. The MAC indicates this by setting the EMAC_TXTMSTAT_NSEC.TXTSSMIS bit. When EMAC_TM_CTL.TXTSSTSM = 0, the MAC ignores the time stamp status of current packet if the time stamp status of previous packet is not read by the software. The MAC indicates this by setting the EMAC_TXTMSTAT_NSEC.TXTSSMIS bit. 0 Disable                          |
| 19 (R/W)           | CSC         | Enable Checksum Correction During OST for PTP Over UDP/IPv4 Packets. When the EMAC_TM_CTL.CSC bit is set, the last two bytes of PTP message sent over UDP/IPv4 is updated to keep the UDP checksum correct, for changes made to origin time stamp and/or correction field as part of one step time stamp operation. The application forms the packet with these two dummy bytes. When cleared (=0), no updates are done to keep the UDP checksum correct. The application forms the packet with UDP checksum configured to 0. |
| 19 (R/W)           | CSC         | 0 Checksum Correction During OST for PTP Over UDP/IPv4 Packets is Disabled                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |

| 19 (R/W)           | CSC         |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |

## Time Stamp Egress Asymmetry Correction Register

The EMAC\_TM\_EGASYM\_CORR register contains the egress asymmetry correction value to be used while updating the correction field in PDelay\_Req PTP messages.

Figure 28-168: EMAC\_TM\_EGASYM\_CORR Register Diagram

![Image](31_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_(EMAC)_artifacts/image_000167_dd560c107bcc72090ed28aa8c05c2cfed6349178b36184ebf86bc3c0aec28d92.png)

Table 28-223: EMAC\_TM\_EGASYM\_CORR Register Fields

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
|--------------------|------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 31:0 (R/W)         | OSTEAC     | One-Step Time Stamp Egress Asymmetry Correction. The EMAC_TM_EGASYM_CORR.OSTEAC field contains the egress path asymmetry value to be subtracted from correctionField of Pdelay_Resp PTP packet. The program- med value must be the negated value in units of nanoseconds multiplied by 2 16 . For example, if the required correction is +2.5 ns, the programmed value must be 0xFFFD_8000, which is the 2's complement of 0x0002_8000(2.5 * 216). Similarly, if the required correction is -3.3 ns, the programmed value is 0x0003_4CCC (3.3 * 216). |

## Time Stamp Ingress Asymmetry Correction Register

The EMAC\_TM\_INGASYM\_CORR register contains the Ingress Asymmetry Correction value to be used while updating correction field in PDelay\_Resp PTP messages.

![Image](31_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_(EMAC)_artifacts/image_000171_030b99e65caea9306b96326e1e1a9df90612ea818ddfe6af73c7c1791b22570f.png)

|--------------------|------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 31:0 (R/W)         | OSTIAC     | One-Step Time Stamp Ingress Asymmetry Correction. The EMAC_TM_INGASYM_CORR.OSTIAC field contains the ingress path asymme- try value to be added to correctionField of Pdelay_Resp PTP packet. The programmed value should be in units of nanoseconds and multiplied by 2 16 . For example, 2.5 ns is represented as 0x00028000. The value can also be negative, which is represented in 2's complement form with bit 31 representing the sign bit. |

## Time Stamp Status Register

All bits except bits[27:25] are cleared when the application reads the EMAC\_TM\_STAT register.

![Image](31_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_(EMAC)_artifacts/image_000175_effefb7f9df57c41f9fa8dae13122854775bed56c25d155c405c384ff5bcc42b.png)

A value equal to the selected depth of FIFO (4, 8, or 16) indicates that the Auxiliary Snapshot FIFO is full. These bits are cleared (to 00000) when the Auxiliary snapshot FIFO clear bit is set. The EMAC_TM_STAT.ATSNS bit is valid only if the Add IEEE 1588 Auxiliary Snapshot option is selected. |

When more than one bit is set at the same time, it means that corresponding auxiliary triggers were sampled at the same clock. These bits are applicable only if the number of auxiliary snapshots is more than one. One bit is assigned for each trigger as shown in the following list: - Bit 16: Auxiliary trigger 0 - Bit 17: Auxiliary trigger 1 - Bit 18: Auxiliary trigger 2 - Bit 19: Auxiliary trigger 3 The software can read this register to find the triggers that are set when the time stamp is taken. |

## MAC Transmit Time Domain Increment Register

The EMAC\_MAC\_TX\_DOMAIN\_TIME\_INCR register indicates the increment value of the PTP time maintained in transmit clock domain that is used for time stamping.

Figure 28-179: EMAC\_MAC\_TX\_DOMAIN\_TIME\_INCR Register Diagram

![Image](31_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_(EMAC)_artifacts/image_000178_a665361ce449a63708c302a0f8acf911321357022d334082152e4d10c1d13573.png)

Table 28-234: EMAC\_MAC\_TX\_DOMAIN\_TIME\_INCR Register Fields

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
|--------------------|------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 31:16 (R/W)        | TXNS       | . Transmit Domain Time Increment Value in Nanoseconds. This field indicates the Nanosecond part of the increment value of the PTP time maintained in Transmit clock domain that is used for timestamping. For example, when operating in 2.5G speed the clock period is 3.2ns, so for Digital Rollover mode the TXNS and RXSNS fields must be programmed with 3 and (0.2*256)=51 respectively. In Binary Rollover mode, 3/0.466=6.44 and 0.2+0.44=0.64, so TXNS and TXSNS fields must be pro- grammed with 6 and (0.64*256)=164 respectively. When both TXSNS and TXNS fields are all-zeros, the fixed value based on operating speed is used for PTP time increment in Transmit clock domain. |
| 15:8 (R/W)         | TXSNS      | . Transmit Domain Time Increment Value in Sub-Nanoseconds. This field indicates the Sub-Nanosecond part of the increment value of the PTP time maintained in Transmit clock domain that is used for timestamping. This field has granularity of 1/256 ns. When both TXSNS and TXNS fields are all-zeros, the fixed value based on operating speed is used for PTP time increment in Transmit clock domain.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |

## Transmit Time Stamp Status Nanoseconds Register

The EMAC\_TXTMSTAT\_NSEC register contains the nanosecond part of time stamp captured for transmit packets when Tx status is disabled. The EMAC\_TXTMSTAT\_NSEC register, along with EMAC\_TXTMSTAT\_SEC, gives the 64-bit time stamp captured for the PTP packet successfully transmitted by the MAC. This value is considered to be read by the application when the last byte of the EMAC\_TXTMSTAT\_NSEC register is read. In the little-endian mode, this means when bits[31:24] are read; in big-endian mode, bits[7:0] are read. If the application does not read these registers and time stamp of another packet is captured, then either the current time stamp is lost (overwritten) or the new time stamp is lost (dropped), depending on the configuration of the EMAC\_TM\_CTL.TXTSSTSM bit. The status bit EMAC\_TM\_STAT.TXTSSIS is set when the MAC transmitter captures the time stamp.

Figure 28-180: EMAC\_TXTMSTAT\_NSEC Register Diagram

![Image](31_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_(EMAC)_artifacts/image_000179_67125829d370a0e6966bdacaa4410f160ecb1a48e95b824f88f05e716ef5017e.png)

When the EMAC_TXTMSTAT_NSEC.TXTSSMIS bit is set, it indicates one of the following: The time stamp of the current packet is ignored if EMAC_TM_CTL.TXTSSTSM = 0. The time stamp of the previous packet is overwritten with time stamp of the current packet if EMAC_TM_CTL.TXTSSTSM = 1. Access restriction applies. Clears on read. Self-set to 1 on internal event. 0 Status Not Detected |
| 30:0 (R/NW)        | TXTSSLO    | Transmit Time Stamp Status Low. The EMAC_TXTMSTAT_NSEC.TXTSSLO field contains the 31 bits of the nanosec- onds field of the transmit packet's captured time stamp.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |

## VLAN Hash Table Register

When EMAC\_VLANTAG\_CTL.VTHM = 1, the 16-bit EMAC\_VLAN\_HASHTBL register is used for group address filtering based on the VLAN tag. For hash filtering, the content of the 16-bit VLAN tag or 12-bit VLAN ID (based on EMAC\_VLANTAG\_CTL.ETV) in the incoming packet is passed through the CRC logic. The upper four bits of the calculated hash value are used to index the contents of the VLAN hash table. For example, hash value of 4b'1000 selects bit 8 of the VLAN hash table.

The hash value of the destination address is calculated in the following way:

1. Calculate the 32-bit CRC for the VLAN tag or ID (For steps to calculate CRC32, see Section 3.2.8 of IEEE 802.3).
2. Perform bitwise reversal for the value obtained in step 1.
3. Take the upper four bits from the value obtained in step 2. The VLAN hash table register is configured to be double-synchronized to the (G)MII clock domain, the synchronization is triggered only when bits[15:8] (in little-endian mode) or bits[7:0] (in big-endian mode) of this register are written.

Consecutive writes to this register should be performed after at least four clock cycles in the (G)MII clock domain.

![Image](31_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_(EMAC)_artifacts/image_000181_13c7ce2ecdbd1c004278ada2342ca62e2126ea109079954dd4dc2d25c77b3891.png)

| 15:0               | VLHT       | VLAN Hash Table.                                                      |
| (R/W)              |            | The EMAC_VLAN_HASHTBL.VLHT field contains the 16-bit VLAN Hash Table. |

The EMAC_VLAN_INCL.VLC field indicates the VLAN tag control in transmit packets. 2'b00: No VLAN tag deletion, insertion, or replacement 2'b01: VLAN tag deletion The MAC removes the VLAN type (bytes 13 and 14) and VLAN tag (bytes 15 and 16) of all transmitted packets with VLAN tags. 2'b10: VLAN tag insertion The MAC inserts VLT in bytes 15 and 16 of the packet after inserting the Type value (0x8100 or 0x88a8) in bytes 13 and 14. This operation is performed on all transmitted packets, irrespective of whether they already have a VLAN tag. 2'b11: VLAN tag replacement The MAC replaces VLT in bytes 15 and 16 of all VLAN-type transmitted packets (Bytes 13 and 14 are 0x8100 or 0x88a8). Note: Changes to this field take effect only on the start of a packet. If this field is written when a packet is being transmitted, only the subsequent packet can use the updated value, that is, the current packet does not use the updated value. |
| 15:0 (R/W)         | VLT        | VLAN Tag for Transmit Packets. The EMAC_VLAN_INCL.VLT field contains the value of the VLAN tag to be inserted or replaced. The value must only be changed when the transmit lines are inactive or during the initialization phase. Bits[15:13] are the User Priority field, Bit 12 is the CFI/DEI field, and Bits[11:0] are the VID field in the VLAN tag. The following list describes the bits of this field: Bits[15:13]: User Priority Bit 12: Canonical Format Indicator (CFI) or Drop Eligible Indicator (DEI) Bits[11:0]: VLAN Identifier (VID) field of VLAN tag                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |

## VLAN Tag Control Register

The EMAC\_VLANTAG\_CTL register contains control and status bits for VLAN filtering operation. It is also used for indirect addressing. It contains the address offset, command type and busy bit for CSR access of the per VLAN tag registers.

When the EMAC_VLANTAG_CTL.VTHM bit is set, the most significant four bits of CRC of VLAN tag are used to index the content of the EMAC_VLAN_HASHTBL_REGn. A value of 1 in the VLAN hash table register, corresponding to the index, indicates that the packet matched the VLAN hash table. When EMAC_VLANTAG_CTL.ETV = 1, the CRC of the 12-bit VLAN Identifier (VID) is used for comparison. When EMAC_VLANTAG_CTL.ETV = 0, the CRC of the 16-bit VLAN tag is used for comparison. ## VLAN Tag Indirect Access Data Register

The EMAC\_VLANTAG\_DAT register holds the read/write data for Indirect Access of the Per VLAN Tag registers. During the read access, this field contains valid read data only after the OB bit is reset. During the write access, this field should be valid prior to EMAC\_VLANTAG\_CTL.OB = 1

## MMC Receive FPE Interrupt Status Register

The EMAC\_MMC\_FPE\_RXINT register maintains the interrupts generated from all FPE-related receive statistics counters. The EMAC\_MMC\_FPE\_RXINT register maintains the interrupts generated when transmit statistic counters reach half their maximum values (0x8000\_0000 for the 32-bit counter and 0x8000 for 16-bit counter), and when they cross their maximum values (0xFFFF\_FFFF for 32-bit counter and 0xFFFF for 16-bit counter). When the Counter Stop Rollover is set, the interrupts are set but the counter remains at all-ones.

The EMAC\_MMC\_FPE\_RXINT register is a 32-bit register. An interrupt bit is cleared when the respective MMC counter that caused the interrupt is read. The least significant byte lane (Bits[7:0]) of the respective counter must be read to clear the interrupt bit.

Figure 28-188: EMAC\_MMC\_FPE\_RXINT Register Diagram

![Image](31_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_(EMAC)_artifacts/image_000187_99df73580ec4260c91ed81a7a8ac0afb165ff6fe125c4323446aad612b108ea1.png)

Self-set to 1 on internal event. Exists when any one of the RX/TX MMCcounters are enabled during FPE-enabled configuration. | MMCRxFPE Fragment Counter Interrupt Status. ## MMC Receive FPE Interrupt Mask Register

The EMAC\_MMC\_FPE\_RXIMSK register maintains the masks for interrupts generated from all FPE-related receive statistics counters. The EMAC\_MMC\_FPE\_RXIMSK register is 32 bit wide.

## MMC Transmit FPE Interrupt Status Register

The EMAC\_MMC\_FPE\_TXINT register maintains the interrupts generated from all FPE related T ransmit statistics counters. The MMC FPE Transmit Interrupt register maintains the interrupts generated when transmit statistic counters reach half their maximum values (0x8000\_0000 for 32 bit counter and 0x8000 for 16 bit counter), and when they cross their maximum values (0xFFFF\_FFFF for 32-bit counter and 0xFFFF for 16-bit counter). When Counter Stop Rollover is set, the interrupts are set but the counter remains at all-ones. The MMC FPE Transmit Interrupt register is a 32 bit register. An interrupt bit is cleared when the respective MMC counter that caused the interrupt is read. The least significant byte lane (Bits[7:0]) of the respective counter must be read to clear the interrupt bit.

## MMC Transmit FPE Interrupt Mask Register

The EMAC\_MMC\_FPE\_TXIMSK register maintains the masks for interrupts generated from all FPE related Transmit statistics counters. The MMC Receive Interrupt Mask register maintains the masks for the interrupts generated when FPE related receive statistic counters reach half of their maximum value or the maximum values. The EMAC\_MMC\_FPE\_TXIMSK register is 32 bit wide.

## MMC Receive IPC Interrupt Status Register

The EMAC\_MMC\_IPC\_RXINT register maintains the interrupt that the receive IPC statistic counters generate.

The EMAC\_MMC\_IPC\_RXINT register maintains the interrupts generated when receive IPC statistic counters reach half their maximum values (0x8000\_0000 for 32 bit counter and 0x8000 for 16 bit counter), and when they cross their maximum values (0xFFFF\_FFFF for 32 bit counter and 0xFFFF for 16 bit counter). When Counter Stop Rollover is set, the interrupts are set but the counter remains at all-ones.

The EMAC\_MMC\_IPC\_RXINT register is 32 bit wide. When the MMC IPC counter that caused the interrupt is read, its corresponding interrupt bit is cleared. The counter's least-significant byte lane (Bits[7:0]) must be read to clear the interrupt bit.

## MMC Receive IPC Interrupt Mask Register

The EMAC\_MMC\_IPC\_RXIMSK register maintains the mask for the interrupt generated from the receive IPC statistic counters.

The MMC Receive Checksum Off load Interrupt Mask register maintains the masks for the interrupts generated when the receive IPC (Checksum Off load) statistic counters reach half their maximum value, and when they reach their maximum values. The EMAC\_MMC\_IPC\_RXIMSK register is 32 bits wide.

## MMC Receive Interrupt Status Register

The EMAC\_MMC\_RXINT register maintains the interrupts generated from all receive statistics counters when the following occurs:

Receive statistic counters reach half of their maximum values (0x8000\_0000 for 32-bit counter and 0x8000 for 16-bit counter).

Receive statistic counters cross their maximum values (0xFFFF\_FFFF for 32-bit counter and 0xFFFF for 16-bit counter).

When the Counter Stop Rollover is set, interrupts are set but the counter remains at all-ones. The EMAC\_MMC\_RXINT register is a 32 bit register. An interrupt bit is cleared when the respective MMC counter that caused the interrupt is read. The least significant byte lane (Bits[7:0]) of the respective counter must be read to clear the interrupt bit.

Note: R\_SS\_RC means that this register bit is set internally, and it is cleared when the counter register is read.

## MMC Receive Interrupt Mask Register

The EMAC\_MMC\_RXIMSK register maintains the masks for the interrupts generated when receive statistic counters reach half of their maximum value or the maximum values.

The EMAC\_MMC\_RXIMSK register is 32 bit wide.

## MMC Transmit Interrupt Status Register

The EMAC\_MMC\_TXINT register maintains the interrupts generated from all transmit statistics counters when transmit statistic counters reach half their maximum values (0x8000\_0000 for 32 bit counter and 0x8000 for 16 bit counter), and when they cross their maximum values (0xFFFF\_FFFF for 32-bit counter and 0xFFFF for 16-bit counter).

When Counter Stop Rollover is set, the interrupts are set but the counter remains at all-ones.

The EMAC\_MMC\_TXINT register is a 32-bit register. An interrupt bit is cleared when the respective MMC counter that caused the interrupt is read.

The least significant byte lane (bits[7:0]) of the respective counter must be read to clear the interrupt bit.

| 0 (R/NW)           | TXGBOCTIS  | MMCTransmit Good Bad Octet Counter Interrupt Status. The EMAC_MMC_TXINT.TXGBOCTIS bit is set when the EMAC_TX_OCNT_GB register reaches half of the maximum value or the maximum value. Access restriction applies. Clears on read. Self-set to 1 on internal event. 0 MMCTransmit Good Bad Octet Counter Interrupt                        |

## MMC Transmit Interrupt Mask Register

The EMAC\_MMC\_TXIMSK register maintains the masks for interrupts generated from all transmit statistics counters.

The EMAC\_MMC\_TXIMSK register maintains the masks for the interrupts generated when the transmit statistic counters reach half of their maximum value or the maximum values. The EMAC\_MMC\_TXIMSK register is 32 bits wide.

## EST Control Register

The EMAC\_EST\_CTL register controls the operation of Enhancements to Scheduled Transmission (EST) (IEEE802.1Qbv).

Figure 28-204: EMAC\_EST\_CTL Register Diagram

![Image](31_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_(EMAC)_artifacts/image_000203_dc745e5b83ba6729cd991d5951dafd548e1e18d971597d5c9b43fb802b7156eb.png)

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
|--------------------|------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 31:24 (R/W)        | PTOV       | PTP Time Offset Value. The EMAC_EST_CTL.PTOV field indicates the value of the PTP clock period multi- plied by 6 in nanoseconds. This value is needed to avoid transmission overruns at the beginning of the installation of a new GCL.                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| 23:12 (R/W)        | CTOV       | Current Time Offset Value. The EMAC_EST_CTL.CTOV field provides a 12 bit time offset value in nano second that is added to the current time to compensate for all the implementation pipeline delays such as the CDC sync delay, buffering delays, data path delays and so on. This offset helps to ensure that the impact of gate controls is visible on the line exactly at the pre-determined schedule (or as close to the schedule as possible). |

## EST Frame Size Capture Register

The EMAC\_EST\_FRMSZ\_CAP register captures the frame size and queue number of the first occurrence of the frame size-related error. Upon clearing, it captures the data of immediate next occurrence of a similar error.

Queue Number of HLBF

Figure 28-206: EMAC\_EST\_FRMSZ\_CAP Register Diagram

![Image](31_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_(EMAC)_artifacts/image_000205_dc0fd86521cfe069d3b30159398945d3b8601644feb760f62dd34a3731be9eae.png)

Table 28-261: EMAC\_EST\_FRMSZ\_CAP Register Fields

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
|--------------------|------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 18:16 (R/NW)       | HBFQ       | Queue Number of HLBF. The EMAC_EST_FRMSZ_CAP.HBFQ field indicates the binary value of the of the first queue (number) experiencing HLBF error (see HLBF field of status register). Value once written is not altered by any subsequent queue errors of similar nature. Once cleared the queue number of the next occurring HLBF error is captured. The width is based on the number of Tx queues configured; remaining bits are read-only. The EMAC_EST_FRMSZ_CAP.HBFQ field is cleared when the EMAC_EST_FRMSZ_ERR register is all zeros. |
| 14:0 (R/NW)        | HBFS       | Frame Size of HLBF. The EMAC_EST_FRMSZ_CAP.HBFS field indicates the frame size of the drop- ped frame related to queue number indicated in EMAC_EST_FRMSZ_CAP.HBFQ field. The contents of the register is considered invalid, if the EMAC_EST_FRMSZ_CAP.HBFS field is zero. The EMAC_EST_FRMSZ_CAP.HBFS field cleared when the EMAC_EST_FRMSZ_ERR register is all zeros.                                                                                                                                                                   |

## EST Gate Control List Control Register

The EMAC\_EST\_GCL\_CTL register provides the control information for reading/writing to the gate control lists.

Figure 28-208: EMAC\_EST\_GCL\_CTL Register Diagram

![Image](31_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_(EMAC)_artifacts/image_000207_027c7aaf6a0ba3690f87e0cb20def9fdc7ff48079147714aed2ba740d8f13b26.png)

|--------------------|------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 15:8 (R/W)         | ADDR       | Gate Control List Address. When set (=1), the EMAC_EST_GCL_CTL.ADDR field indicates the address (row number) of the GCL at which the R/W operation must be performed. By de- fault, the GCL pointed by EMAC_EST_STAT.SWOL is selected for R/W. How- ever, if EMAC_EST_GCL_CTL.DBGM =1, a debug mode access is given to R/W from EMAC_EST_GCL_CTL.DBGB . The width of this field is dependent on DWC_EQOS_EST_DEP; unused bits should be treated as read only. Gate Control List Related Registers Address: (GCRA when GCRR =1). By default, the GCL-related register set pointed by EMAC_EST_STAT.SWOL is selected for R/W. However, if EMAC_EST_GCL_CTL.DBGM =1, debug mode access is given to R/W from EMAC_EST_GCL_CTL.DBGB . Lower 3 bits are only used in this mode, higher order bits are treated as dont care. 000: BTR Low (31:0) 001: BTR High (63:31) 010: CTR Low (31:0) 011: CTR High (39:32) 100: TER (31:0) 101: LLR (8:0) Others: Reserved |

## EST Status Register

The EMAC\_EST\_STAT register provides status information related to Enhancements to Scheduled T ransmission (EST) (IEEE802.1Qbv).

Figure 28-212: EMAC\_EST\_STAT Register Diagram

![Image](31_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_(EMAC)_artifacts/image_000211_152829e5922cdb634e8848242c173de67f906498c6fc053de0901a67ffaa5a9b.png)

| 19:16 (R/NW)       | CGSN       | Current GCL Slot Number. The EMAC_EST_STAT.CGSN field indicates the slot number of the GCL list. Slot number is a modulo 16 count of the GCL list loops executed so far. Even if a new GCL list is installed, the count is incremental.                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| 15:8 (R/NW)        | BTRL       | BTR Error Loop Count. The EMAC_EST_STAT.BTRL field provides the minimum count (N) for which the equation Current Time =< New BTR + (N * New Cycle Time) becomes true.N = "11111111" indicates the iterations exceeded the value of 128 and the hardware was not able to update New BTR to be equal to or greater than Current Time. Software intervention is needed to update the new BTR. Value is cleared when EMAC_EST_STAT.BTRE = 0. |

## Frame Preemption Advance Register

The EMAC\_FPE\_ADV register contains the hold and release advance time.

Figure 28-213: EMAC\_FPE\_ADV Register Diagram

![Image](31_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_(EMAC)_artifacts/image_000212_2085813f858279d970932340b33fb936f499d3a62bd745b7ea0ec9911f6ab682.png)

Table 28-268: EMAC\_FPE\_ADV Register Fields

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
|--------------------|------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 31:16 (R/W)        | RADV       | Release Advance. The EMAC_FPE_ADV.RADV field indicates the maximum time in nanoseconds that can elapse between issuing a RELEASE to the MAC and the MAC being ready to resume transmission of preemptable frames, in the absence of there being any express frames available for transmission.  |
| 15:0 (R/W)         | HADV       | Hold Advance. The EMAC_FPE_ADV.HADV field indicates the maximum time in nanoseconds that can elapse between issuing a HOLD to the MAC, and the MAC ceasing to transmit any preemptable frame that is in the process of transmission or any preemptable frames that are queued for transmission. |

## MTL Frame Preemption Control and Status Register

The EMAC\_FPE\_CTRLSTS register controls the operation of, and provides status for frame preemption (IEEE802.1Qbu/802.3br).

Figure 28-214: EMAC\_FPE\_CTRLSTS Register Diagram

![Image](31_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_(EMAC)_artifacts/image_000213_3f0668e4c8c3f0438225bdde2faf17b7623db6f9641575da244ae965b4b4ec53.png)

Table 28-269: EMAC\_FPE\_CTRLSTS Register Fields

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
|--------------------|------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 28 (R/NW)          | HRS        | Hold/Release Status. The EMAC_FPE_CTRLSTS.HRS bit indicates whether a set-and-hold MAC oper- ation was last executed and the pMAC is in hold state or a set-and-release MAC operation was last executed and the pMAC is in the release state.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| 15:8 (R/W)         | PEC        | Preemption Classification. When set (=1), the EMAC_FPE_CTRLSTS.PEC field indicates that the correspond- ing queue must be classified as preemptable, when '0' queue is classified as express. When both EST (Qbv) and preemption are enabled, queue 0 is always assumed to be preemptable. When EST (Qbv) is enabled, queues categorized as preemptable here are                                                                                                                                        |
| 7 (R/W)            | LBHT       | Level Based Hold Transition. When EMAC_FPE_CTRLSTS.LBHT =1, the bit enables a hold operation in the second row of the EST GCL when a hold request is set in the second GCL row for the first loop of a new GCL, even though hold request is also set in the first GCL row. This is a deviation from the original behavior, where a transition from a release request to a hold request is required. When cleared (= 0), enables hold operation only on transition from release request to hold request. |

Table 28-269: EMAC\_FPE\_CTRLSTS Register Fields (Continued)

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
|--------------------|------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 1:0 (R/W)          | AFSZ       | Additional Fragment Size. The EMAC_FPE_CTRLSTS.AFSZ field indicates, in units of 64 bytes, the mini- mum number of bytes over 64 bytes required in non-final fragments of preempted frames. The minimum non-final fragment size is (AFSZ +1) * 64 bytes. |

## Receive Queue Control Register

The EMAC\_RQ0\_CTL register controls the receive arbitration and passing of received packets to the application.

Figure 28-219: EMAC\_RQ0\_CTL Register Diagram

![Image](31_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_(EMAC)_artifacts/image_000218_c0d11e8d429275fb664e8190f62f1ca45bdb4db05a5c41f9293912316850e394.png)

Table 28-274: EMAC\_RQ0\_CTL Register Fields

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name      | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
|--------------------|---------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 3 (R/W)            | RXQ_FRM_ARBIT | Receive Queue Packet Arbitration. When the EMAC_RQ0_CTL.RXQ_FRM_ARBIT bit is set, the EMAC module drives the packet data to the ARI interface such that the entire packet data of currently-select- ed queue is transmitted before switching to other queue. When EMAC_RQ0_CTL.RXQ_FRM_ARBIT = 0, the EMAC module drives the packet data to the ARI interface such that the following amount of data of currently- selected queue is transmitted before switching to other queue: - PBL amount of data or - Complete data of a packet The status and the time stamp are not a part of the PBL data. Therefore, the EMAC module drives the complete status (including time stamp status) during first PBL request for the packet (in store-and-forward mode) or the last PBL request for the packet (in threshold mode). |
| 3 (R/W)            |               | 0 Receive Queue Packet Arbitration is Disabled                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| 3 (R/W)            |               | 1 Receive Queue Packet Arbitration is Enabled                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |

Table 28-274: EMAC\_RQ0\_CTL Register Fields (Continued)

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
|--------------------|------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 2:0 (R/W)          | RXQ_WEGT   | Receive Queue Weight. The EMAC_RQ0_CTL.RXQ_WEGT field indicates the weight assigned to the Rx queue 0. The field must be programmed with one value less than the required weight, that is, reset value of 0 indicates weight of 1, value of 1 indicates weight of 2, and so on. The weight is used as the number of continuous PBL or packets requests (depending on the RXQ_FRM_ARBIT) allocated to the queue in one arbitration cycle. Note: The change in value of RXQ_WEGT takes effect only after the com- pletion of current service round or when there is change from RAA=SP to RAA=WSP algorithm. This approach is taken so that there is smooth transition. For the EMAC_RQ0_CTL.RXQ_WEGT value to take effect at the start, the EMAC_RQ[n]_CTL registers must be programmed before the EMAC_MTL_OP- MODEregister. |

## Receive Queue 0 Operation Mode Register

The EMAC\_RQ0\_OPMODE register establishes the receive queue operating modes and command.

The RFA and RFD fields are not backward compatible with the RFA and RFD fields of 4.00a release.

Figure 28-222: EMAC\_RQ0\_OPMODE Register Diagram

![Image](31_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_(EMAC)_artifacts/image_000221_eea36c286c164355e8e5e898e403991158a375802f74bf8d5b4bce9186c5b6f2.png)

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
|--------------------|------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 25:20 (R/W)        | RQS        | Receive Queue Size. The EMAC_RQ0_OPMODE.RQS field indicates the size of the allocated receive queues in blocks of 256 bytes. The field is read-write only if the number of Rx queues more than one, the reset value is 0x0 and indicates size of 256 bytes. For example, the value of 0x0 = 256 bytes, 0x1 = 512 bytes and so on. So, program RQS [5:0] = 6'b001111 to allocate queue size of 4096 (4K) bytes. In general, the size of the queue = (RQS+1)*256 bytes. When the number of Rx queues is one, the field is read-only and the configured RX FIFO size in blocks of 256 bytes is reflected in the reset value. |

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
|--------------------|------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 2:0 (R/W)          | RXQ_WEGT   | Receive Queue Weight. The EMAC_RQ[n]_CTL.RXQ_WEGT field indicates the weight assigned to the Rx queue 0. The EMAC_RQ[n]_CTL.RXQ_WEGT field needs to be programmed with one value less than the required weight. For example, a reset value of 0 indicates a weight of 1, a value of 1 indicates weight of 2, and so on. The weight is used as the number of continuous PBL or packets requests (depending on the RXQ_FRM_AR- BIT) allocated to the queue in one arbitration cycle. Note: The change in value of RXQ_WEGT takes effect only after the completion of current service round or when there is change from RAA=SP to RAA=WSP algorithm. This approach is taken so that there is smooth transition. For the RXQ_WEGT value to take effect at the start, the EMAC_RQ[n]_CTL registers must be programmed before the EMAC_MTL_OPMODE register. |
