## Receive Queue n Missed Packet and Overflow Counter Register

The EMAC\_RQ[n]\_MSPKTOF\_CNT register contains the counter for packets missed because of receive queue packet flush and packets discarded because of receive queue overflow.

Figure 28-225: EMAC\_RQ[n]\_MSPKTOF\_CNT Register Diagram

![Image](31_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_(EMAC)_artifacts/image_000224_e8630573dc8a69034ba8d6f9160d78e0452ccfa819fbbc0a4a05fbf91e1effa2.png)

Table 28-280: EMAC\_RQ[n]\_MSPKTOF\_CNT Register Fields

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
|--------------------|------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 27 (R/NW)          | MISCNTOVF  | Missed Packet Counter Overflow Bit. When set, the EMAC_RQ[n]_MSPKTOF_CNT.MISCNTOVF bit indicates that the Rx queue missed packet counter crossed the maximum limit. Access restriction applies. Clears (=0) on read. Self-set to 1 on internal event. 0 Overflow Not Detected                                                                                                      |
| 26:16 (R/NW)       | MISPKTCNT  | Missed Packet Counter. The EMAC_RQ[n]_MSPKTOF_CNT.MISPKTCNT field indicates the number of packets missed by the EMAC module because the application asserted EMAC_DMA[n]_RXCTL.RPF for this queue. This counter is incremented by 1 when the DMAdiscards the packet because of buffer unavailability. Access restriction applies. Clears on read. Self-set to 1 on internal event. |
| 11 (R/NW)          | OVFCNTOVF  | Overflow Counter Overflow Bit. When set, the EMAC_RQ[n]_MSPKTOF_CNT.OVFCNTOVF bit indicates that the Rx queue overflow packet counter field crossed the maximum limit. Access restriction applies. Clears on read. Self-set to 1 on internal event. 0 Overflow Not Detected                                                                                                        |
| 11 (R/NW)          | OVFCNTOVF  | 1 Overflow Detected                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |

Table 28-280: EMAC\_RQ[n]\_MSPKTOF\_CNT Register Fields (Continued)

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
|--------------------|------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 10:0 (R/NW)        | OVFPKTCNT  | Overflow Packet Counter. The EMAC_RQ[n]_MSPKTOF_CNT.OVFPKTCNT field indicates the number of packets discarded by the EMAC module because of receive queue overflow. This counter is incremented each time the EMAC module discards an incoming packet because of overflow. Access restriction applies. Clears on read. Self-set to 1 on internal event. |

## Receive Queue n Operation Mode Register

The EMAC\_RQ[n]\_OPMODE register establishes the receive queue operating modes and command.

The RFA and RFD fields are not backward compatible with the RFA and RFD fields of 4.00a release

Figure 28-226: EMAC\_RQ[n]\_OPMODE Register Diagram

![Image](31_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_(EMAC)_artifacts/image_000225_39428afa12c4b7e80a6471e3893daea8b16e04bcf27006bb9cb43fa7e681e2ea.png)

Table 28-281: EMAC\_RQ[n]\_OPMODE Register Fields

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
|--------------------|------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 25:20 (R/W)        | RQS        | Receive Queue Size. The EMAC_RQ[n]_OPMODE.RQS field indicates the size of the allocated receive queues in blocks of 256 bytes. The field is read-write only if the number of Rx queues is more than one; the reset value is 0x0 and indicates size of 256 bytes. For example, a value of 0x0 = 256 bytes, 0x1 = 512 bytes and so on. Program RQS [5:0] = 6'b001111 to allocate queue size of 4096 (4K) bytes. In general, the size of the queue = (RQS+1)*256 bytes. When the number of Rx queues is one, the field is read-only and the configured RX FIFO size in blocks of 256 bytes is reflected in the reset value. |

Table 28-281: EMAC\_RQ[n]\_OPMODE Register Fields (Continued)

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
|--------------------|------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 18:14 (R/W)        | RFD        | Threshold for Deactivating Flow Control. The EMAC_RQ[n]_OPMODE.RFD field indicates the threshold (fill-level of Rx queue) at which the flow control is deasserted after activation (in half-duplex and full-duplex modes): - 0: Full minus 1 KB, that is, FULL 1 KB - 1: Full minus 1.5 KB, that is, FULL 1.5 KB - 2: Full minus 2 KB, that is, FULL 2 KB - 3: Full minus 2.5 KB, that is, FULL 2.5 KB - ... - 30: Full minus 16 KB, that is, FULL 16 KB - 31: Full minus 16.5 KB, that is, FULL 16.5 KB The deassertion is effective only after flow control is asserted. Note: The value must be programmed in such a way to make sure that the threshold is a positive number. When EMAC_RQ[n]_OPMODE.EHFC =1, these values are applicable only when the Rx queue size determined by the EMAC_RQ[n]_OPMODE.RQS field, is equal to or greater than 4 KB. For a given queue size, the values ranges between 0 and the encoding for FULL minus (QSIZE - 0.5 KB) and all other values are illegal. Here, the term FULL and QSIZE refers to the queue size determined by the EMAC_RQ[n]_OPMODE.RQS field. |
| 12:8 (R/W)         | RFA        | Threshold for Activating Flow Control. The EMAC_RQ[n]_OPMODE.RFA field indicates the threshold (fill-level of Rx queue) at which the flow control is activated (in half-duplex and full-duplex modes). For more information on encoding for this field, see RFD.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| 7 (R/W)            | EHFC       | Hardware Flow Control Enable. When the EMAC_RQ[n]_OPMODE.EHFC bit is set (=1), the flow control signal operation, based on the fill-level of Rx queue, is enabled. When cleared (=0), the flow control operation is disabled. 0 Disabled                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| 7 (R/W)            | EHFC       | 1 Enabled                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |

Table 28-281: EMAC\_RQ[n]\_OPMODE Register Fields (Continued)

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
|--------------------|------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 6 (R/W)            | DIS_TCP_EF | Disable Dropping of TCP/IP Checksum Error Packets. When the EMAC_RQ[n]_OPMODE.DIS_TCP_EF bit is set (=1), the MAC does not drop the packets which only have the errors detected by the receive checksum offload engine. Such packets have errors only in the encapsulated payload. There are no errors (including FCS error) in the Ethernet packet received by the MAC. When EMAC_RQ[n]_OPMODE.DIS_TCP_EF = 0, all error packets are dropped if EMAC_RQ[n]_OPMODE.FEP = 0. 0 Enabled                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| 5 (R/W)            | RSF        | Receive Queue Store and Forward. When the EMAC_RQ[n]_OPMODE.RSF bit is set (=1), the EMAC module reads a packet from the Rx queue only after the complete packet has been written to it, ignor- ing the EMAC_RQ[n]_OPMODE.RTC field. When EMAC_RQ[n]_OPMODE.RSF = 0, the Rx queue operates in the threshold (cut-through) mode, subject to the threshold specified by the EMAC_RQ[n]_OPMODE.RTC field. 0 Disabled                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| 4 (R/W)            | FEP        | Forward Error Packets. When EMAC_RQ[n]_OPMODE.FEP = 0, the Rx queue drops packets with error status (CRC error, GMII_ER, watchdog timeout, or overflow). However, if the start byte (write) pointer of a packet is already transferred to the read controller side (in threshold mode), the packet is not dropped. When the EMAC_RQ[n]_OPMODE.FEP bit is set, all packets except the runt error packets are forwarded to the application or DMA. If the RSF bit is set and the Rx queue overflows when a partial packet is written, the packet is dropped irrespective of the setting of the EMAC_RQ[n]_OPMODE.FEP bit. However, if the RSF bit is reset and the Rx queue overflows when a partial packet is written, a partial packet might be forwarded to the application or DMA. 0 Disabled |
| 4 (R/W)            |            | 1 Enabled                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| 4 (R/W)            |            |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |

Table 28-281: EMAC\_RQ[n]\_OPMODE Register Fields (Continued)

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
|--------------------|------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 3 (R/W)            | FUP        | Forward Undersized Good Packets. When the EMAC_RQ[n]_OPMODE.FUP bit is set, the Rx queue forwards the un- dersized good packets (packets with no error and length less than 64 bytes), including pad-bytes and CRC. When EMAC_RQ[n]_OPMODE.FUP = 0, the Rx queue drops all packets of less than 64 bytes, unless a packet is already transferred because of the lower value of Rx threshold, for example, RTC = 01.                                                                                                                                |
| 1:0 (R/W)          | RTC        | 1 Enabled Receive Queue Threshold Control. The EMAC_RQ[n]_OPMODE.RTC field indicates the threshold level of the MTL Rx queue (in bytes). The received packet is transferred to the application or DMAwhen the packet size within the MTL Rx queue is larger than the threshold. In addition, full packets with length less than the threshold are automatically transferred. The EMAC_RQ[n]_OPMODE.RTC field is valid only when the RSF bit is zero. The EMAC_RQ[n]_OPMODE.RTC field is ignored when the RSF bit is set (=1). 0 64 1 32 2 96 3 128 |

The EMAC\_RXQ\_DMA\_MAP0 register is reserved in EQOS-CORE and EQOS-MTL configurations.

Figure 28-227: EMAC\_RXQ\_DMA\_MAP0 Register Diagram

![Image](31_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_(EMAC)_artifacts/image_000226_e445254f13c4666b6e1b19d532881fb27578e0b80a91679f7104006c6efa69e2.png)

When cleared (=0), the EMAC_RXQ_DMA_MAP0.Q3DDMACH bit indicates that the packets received in queue 3 are routed to the DMAchannel programmed in the EMAC_RXQ_DMA_MAP0.Q3MDMACH field. 0 Disable |

Note: The width of this field depends on the number of RX DMAchannels and not all the values might be valid in some configurations. For example, if the number of RX DMAchannels selected is 2, only 000 and 001 are valid, the others are reserved                                   |

## MTL Time Based Scheduling Control Register

The EMAC\_TBS\_CTRL register controls the operation of Time-Based Scheduling (TBS).

Figure 28-229: EMAC\_TBS\_CTRL Register Diagram

![Image](31_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_(EMAC)_artifacts/image_000228_801818b73a5358be3add201378a1593c78b6f9c93190144f0e8cbac232c01474.png)

Table 28-284: EMAC\_TBS\_CTRL Register Fields

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
|--------------------|------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 31:8 (R/W)         | LEOS       | Launch Expiry Offset. The field contains the value in units of 256 nanoseconds that must be added to the launch time to compute the launch expiry time. The value is valid only when EMAC_TBS_CTRL.LEOV = 1. The max value, 999,999,999 ns, should be smaller than the CTR-1 value when ESTM mode is enabled, because this value is a modulo CTR value. |
| 6:4 (R/W)          | LEGOS      | Launch Expiry GSN Offset. The EMAC_TBS_CTRL.LEGOS field indicates the number GSN slots that must be added to the launch GSN to compute the launch expiry time. The value is valid only when EMAC_TBS_CTRL.LEOV = 1.                                                                                                                                     |
| 1 (R/W)            | LEOV       | Launch Expiry Offset Valid. When set (=1), the EMAC_TBS_CTRL.LEOV bit indicates that the EMAC_TBS_CTRL.LEOS field is valid. When not set, it indicates that the launch expiry offset is invalid and the MTL must not check for launch expiry time. LEOS Field is Invalid                                                                                |
| 1 (R/W)            | LEOV       | 0                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| 1 (R/W)            | LEOV       | 1 LEOS Field is Valid                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |

Table 28-284: EMAC\_TBS\_CTRL Register Fields (Continued)

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
|--------------------|------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 0 (R/W)            | ESTM       | EST Offset Mode. When the EMAC_TBS_CTRL.ESTM bit is set, the launch time value used in time based scheduling is interpreted as an EST offset value and is added to the Base Time Register (BTR) of the current list. When cleared (=0), the launch time value is used as an absolute value that should be compared with the system time [39:8]. Disabled |
| 0 (R/W)            | ESTM       | 0                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| 0 (R/W)            | ESTM       | 1 Enabled                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |

## Transmit Queue 0 Debug Register

The EMAC\_TQ0\_DBG register gives the debug status of various blocks related to the transmit queue.

Figure 28-230: EMAC\_TQ0\_DBG Register Diagram

![Image](31_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_(EMAC)_artifacts/image_000229_743d0272993de4cd4eb9cf0a2c6066c8587855f9c193c007df0d480db7a404ad.png)

|--------------------|------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 22:20 (R/NW)       | STXSTSF    | Number of Status Words in Tx Status FIFO of Queue. The EMAC_TQ0_DBG.STXSTSF field indicates the current number of status in the Tx status FIFO of this queue. When EMAC_MTL_OPMODE.DTXSTS = 1, this field does not reflect the number of status words in Tx status FIFO. |
| 18:16 (R/NW)       | PTXQ       | Number of Packets in the Transmit Queue. The EMAC_TQ0_DBG.PTXQ field indicates the current number of packets in the Tx queue. When EMAC_MTL_OPMODE.DTXSTS = 1, this field does not reflect the number of packets in the transmit queue.                                  |
| 5 (R/NW)           | TXSTSFSTS  | MTL Tx Status FIFO Full Status. When set (=1), the EMAC_TQ0_DBG.TXSTSFSTS bit indicates that the MTL Tx status FIFO is full. Therefore, the MTL cannot accept any more packets for transmis- sion.                                                                       |
| 5 (R/NW)           | TXSTSFSTS  | 0 MTL Tx Status FIFO Full Status is Not Detected                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| 5 (R/NW)           | TXSTSFSTS  | 1 MTL Tx Status FIFO Full Status is Detected                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |

When the EMAC_TQ0_DBG.TXQSTS bit is set (=1), it indicates that the MTL Tx queue is not empty and some data is left for transmission.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |

When the EMAC_TQ0_DBG.TXQPAUSED bit is set (=1) and the Rx flow control is enabled, it indicates that the Tx queue is in the Pause condition (in the full-duplex only mode) because of the following: Reception of the PFC packet for the priorities assigned to the Tx queue when PFC is enabled. ## Transmit Queue 0 ETS Status Register

The EMAC\_TQ0\_ETS\_STAT register provides the average traffic transmitted in queue 0.

Figure 28-231: EMAC\_TQ0\_ETS\_STAT Register Diagram

![Image](31_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_(EMAC)_artifacts/image_000230_f2469c0278f0583cbf4f597bbe97aa5498cd357a4fce677b681e525134ef3f01.png)

Table 28-286: EMAC\_TQ0\_ETS\_STAT Register Fields

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
|--------------------|------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 23:0 (R/NW)        | ABS        | Average Bits per Slot. The EMAC_TQ0_ETS_STAT.ABS field contains the average transmitted bits per slot. When the DCB operation is enabled for queue 0, this field is computed over every 10 million bit times slot (4 ms in 2500 Mbps; 10 ms in 1000 Mbps; 100 ms in 100 Mbps). The maximum value is 0x989680. |

## Transmit Queue 0 Operation Mode Register

The EMAC\_TQ0\_OPMODE register establishes the transmit queue operating modes and commands.

![Image](31_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_(EMAC)_artifacts/image_000231_ba276a79827ca7f2aea96b04ae6d312a8018d9bd0419849b4d92a5f865070921.png)

Transmit Queue Size

|--------------------|------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 21:16 (R/W)        | TQS        | Transmit Queue Size. The EMAC_TQ0_OPMODE.TQS field indicates the size of the allocated transmit queues in blocks of 256 bytes. The field is read-write only if the number of Tx queues more than one, the reset value is 0x0 and indicates size of 256 bytes. For example, a value of 0x0 = 256 bytes, 0x1 = 512 bytes and so on. So, program TQS [5:0] = 6'b001111 to allocate queue size of 4096 (4K) bytes. In general, the size of the queue = (TQS+1)*256 bytes. When the number of Tx queues is one, the field is read-only and the configured TX FIFO size in blocks of 256 bytes is reflected in the reset value. | Transmit Queue Size. So, program TQS [5:0] = 6'b001111 to allocate queue size of 4096 (4K) bytes. In general, the size of the queue = (TQS+1)*256 bytes. When the number of Tx queues is one, the field is read-only and the configured TX FIFO size in blocks of 256 bytes is reflected in the reset value. |

| 0 (R/W)            | FTQ        | 1                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | Flush Transmit Queue is Enabled                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |

## Transmit Queue 0 IdleSlopeCredit, Quantum or Weights Register

The EMAC\_TQ0\_QTMWGT register contains the quantum value for Deficit Weighted Round Robin (DWRR), weights for the Weighted Round Robin (WRR), and Weighted Fair Queuing (WFQ) for queue 0.

Figure 28-233: EMAC\_TQ0\_QTMWGT Register Diagram

![Image](31_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_(EMAC)_artifacts/image_000232_27976cc2a3800c8029583e954c2fb4857b025d79816198a73103929905b6e0f1.png)

Table 28-288: EMAC\_TQ0\_QTMWGT Register Fields

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
|--------------------|------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 20:0 (R/W)         | ISCQW      | Quantum or Weights. When the DCB operation is enabled with DWRR algorithm for queue 0 traffic, the EMAC_TQ0_QTMWGT.ISCQW field contains the quantum value in bytes to be added to credit during every queue scanning cycle. The maximum value is 0x1312D0 bytes. When DCB operation is enabled with WFQalgorithm for queue 0 traffic, the EMAC_TQ0_QTMWGT.ISCQW field contains the weight for this queue. The maxi- mum value is 0x3FFF where weight of 0 indicates 100% bandwidth. Bits[20:14] must be written to zero. The higher the programmed weights lesser the bandwidth allocated for the particular transmit queue. This is because the weights are used to compute the packet finish time (weights * packet_size). Lesser the finish time, higher the probability of the packet getting scheduled first and using more bandwidth. When DCB operation or generic queuing operation is enabled with WRR algorithm for queue 0 traffic, this field contains the weight for this queue. The maximum value is 0x64. Bits [20:7] must be written to zero. |

## Transmit Queue 0 Underflow Packet Counter Register

The EMAC\_TQ0\_URFL register contains the counter for packets aborted because of transmit queue underflow and packets missed because of receive queue packet flush.

Figure 28-234: EMAC\_TQ0\_URFL Register Diagram

![Image](31_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_(EMAC)_artifacts/image_000233_fb9540574f9e4a321feaa613705c490c7c5fe9f697ea6cc99bc3de55401cec84.png)

Table 28-289: EMAC\_TQ0\_URFL Register Fields

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
|--------------------|------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 11 (R/NW)          | UFCNTOVF   | Overflow Bit for Underflow Packet Counter. The EMAC_TQ0_URFL.UFCNTOVF bit is set every time the Tx queue Under- flow Packet Counter field overflows, that is, it has crossed the maximum count. In such a scenario, the overflow packet counter is reset to all-zeros and the EMAC_TQ0_URFL.UFCNTOVF bit indicates that the rollover happened. Access restriction applies. Clears on read. Self-set to 1 on internal event. 0 Overflow Not Detected for Underflow Packet Counter |
| 10:0 (R/NW)        | UFFRMCNT   | Underflow Packet Counter. The EMAC_TQ0_URFL.UFFRMCNT field indicates the number of packets aborted by the controller because of Tx queue underflow. This counter is incremented each time the MAC aborts outgoing packet because of underflow. Access restriction applies. Clears on read. Self-set to 1 on internal event.                                                                                                                                                      |

## Transmit Queue n CBS HiCredit Register

The EMAC\_TQ[n]\_HICRDT register contains the HiCredit value required for the credit-based shaper algorithm for the queue.

Figure 28-238: EMAC\_TQ[n]\_HICRDT Register Diagram

![Image](31_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_(EMAC)_artifacts/image_000237_f4a1c474fcb4653427a738ae3a765646abb9e8be965b534d543eccc7869ccbc6.png)

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
|--------------------|------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 28:0 (R/W)         | HC         | HiCredit Value. When the AV feature is enabled, the EMAC_TQ[n]_HICRDT.HC field contains the hiCredit value required for the credit-based shaper algorithm. This is the maximum value that can be accumulated in the credit parameter. It is specified in bits scaled by 1,024. The maximum value is maxInterferenceSize, that is, best-effort maximum packet size (16,384 bytes or 131,072 bits). The value to be specified is 131,072 * 1,024 = 134,217,728 or 0x0800_0000. |

## Transmit Queue n CBS LoCredit Register

The EMAC\_TQ[n]\_LOCRDT register contains the loCredit value required for the credit-based shaper algorithm for the queue.

Figure 28-239: EMAC\_TQ[n]\_LOCRDT Register Diagram

![Image](31_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_(EMAC)_artifacts/image_000238_6f918720c3a779343916aacb98badd7da1447aa79b0f77b5c48ff5eed2571dd6.png)

Table 28-294: EMAC\_TQ[n]\_LOCRDT Register Fields

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
|--------------------|------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 28:0 (R/W)         | LC         | LoCredit Value. When the AV operation is enabled, the EMAC_TQ[n]_LOCRDT.LC field contains the loCredit value required for the credit-based shaper algorithm. This is the mini- mum value that can be accumulated in the credit parameter. It is specified in bits scaled by 1,024. The maximum value to be programmed corresponds to twice the maxFrameSize transmitted from this queue. If the maxFrameSize is 8192 bytes, then (8192*2) * 8 * 1024 = 134,217,728 or 0x0800_0000. Because it is a negative value, the programmed value is the 2's complement of the value, that is, 0x1800_0000. |

## Transmit Queue n IdleSlopeCredit, Quantum or Weights Register

The EMAC\_TQ[n]\_QTMWGT register provides the average traffic transmitted in queue 1.

Figure 28-241: EMAC\_TQ[n]\_QTMWGT Register Diagram

![Image](31_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_(EMAC)_artifacts/image_000240_36f982434752b270bebada4b9402db84b29756ff11ee8bfbc56fd436ebfc73e8.png)

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 20:0 (R/W)         | ISCQW      | IdleSlopeCredit, Quantum or Weights. When AV feature is enabled, the EMAC_TQ[n]_QTMWGT.ISCQW field contains the idleSlopeCredit value required for the credit-based shaper algorithm for queue 1. This is the rate of change of credit in bits per cycle (40 ns for 100 Mbps; 8 ns for 1000 Mbps; 3.2 ns for 2500 Mbps) when the credit is increasing. The software should program the EMAC_TQ[n]_QTMWGT.ISCQW field with computed credit in bits per cycle scaled by 1,024. The maximum value is portTransmitRate, that is, 0x2000 in 1000/2500 Mbps mode and 0x1000 in 100 Mbps mode. Bits[20:14] must be written to zero. Quantum When the DCB operation is enabled with DWRR algorithm for queue 1 traffic, the EMAC_TQ[n]_QTMWGT.ISCQW field field contains the quantum value in bytes to be added to credit during every queue scanning cycle. The maximum value is 0x1312D0 bytes. Weights When DCB operation is enabled with WFQalgorithm for queue 1 traffic, the EMAC_TQ[n]_QTMWGT.ISCQW field contains the weight for this queue. The max- imum value is 0x3FFF where weight of 0 indicates 100% bandwidth. Bits[20:14] must be written to zero. When DCB operation or generic queuing operation is enabled with WRR algorithm for queue 1 traffic, the EMAC_TQ[n]_QTMWGT.ISCQW field contains the weight for this queue. The maximum value is 0x64. Bits [20:7] must be written to zero. Note 1: In multiple queue configuration this field in respective per queue register must be programmed to some non-zero value when multiple queues are enabled or single queue other than Q0 is enabled. The EMAC_TQ[n]_QTMWGT.ISCQW field need not be programmed when only Q0 is enabled. In general, when WRR algorithm is selected a non-zero value must be programmed on both receive and transmit. In receive, the register is EMAC_MTL_OPMODE register. Note 2: For WFQalgorithm, higher the programmed weights lesser the bandwidth allocated for that transmit queue. The finish time is not a function of particular packet alone but it is as per the formula: (previous_finish_time of particular transmit queue + (weights*packet_size)) Note 3: The weights programmed do not correspond to the number of packets but the fraction of bandwidth or time allocated for particular queue with respect to totalBW or time. |

## Transmit Queue n SendSlopeCredit Register

The EMAC\_TQ[n]\_SSCRDT register contains the sendSlope credit value required for the credit-based shaper algorithm for the queue.

Figure 28-242: EMAC\_TQ[n]\_SSCRDT Register Diagram

![Image](31_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_(EMAC)_artifacts/image_000241_ad1f6069f8ac3bc6592438440d451a73d3df9350f8f62e2ccffc410352f4d202.png)

Table 28-297: EMAC\_TQ[n]\_SSCRDT Register Fields

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
|--------------------|------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 13:0 (R/W)         | SSC        | SendSlopeCredit Value. When AV operation is enabled, the EMAC_TQ[n]_SSCRDT.SSC field contains the sendSlopeCredit value required for credit-based shaper algorithm for queue 1. This is the rate of change of credit in bits per cycle (40 ns, 8 ns and 3.2 ns for 100 Mbps, 1000 Mbps and 2500 Mbps respectively) when the credit is decreasing. The software should program this field with computed credit in bits per cycle scaled by 1,024. The maximum value is portTransmitRate, that is, 0x2000 in 1000/2500 Mbps mode and 0x1000 in 100 Mbps mode. The EMAC_TQ[n]_SSCRDT.SSC field should be programmed with absolute sendSlopeCredit value. The credit-based shaper logic subtracts it from the accumulated credit when channel 1 is selected for transmission. |

## Transmit Queue n Underflow Packet Counter Register

The EMAC\_TQ[n]\_URFL register contains the counter for packets aborted because of transmit queue underflow and packets missed because of receive queue packet flush.

Figure 28-243: EMAC\_TQ[n]\_URFL Register Diagram

![Image](31_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_(EMAC)_artifacts/image_000242_fb9540574f9e4a321feaa613705c490c7c5fe9f697ea6cc99bc3de55401cec84.png)

Table 28-298: EMAC\_TQ[n]\_URFL Register Fields

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
|--------------------|------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 11 (R/NW)          | UFCNTOVF   | Overflow Bit for Underflow Packet Counter. The EMAC_TQ[n]_URFL.UFCNTOVF bit is set every time the Tx queue under- flow packet counter field overflows, that is, it has crossed the maximum count. In such a scenario, the overflow packet counter is reset to all-zeros and the EMAC_TQ[n]_URFL.UFCNTOVF bit indicates that the rollover happened. Access restriction applies. Clears on read. Self-set to 1 on internal event. 0 Overflow Not Detected for Underflow Packet Counter |
| 10:0 (R/NW)        | UFFRMCNT   | Underflow Packet Counter. The EMAC_TQ[n]_URFL.UFFRMCNT field indicates the number of packets abort- ed by the controller because of Tx queue underflow. This counter is incremented each time the MAC aborts outgoing packet because of underflow. Access restriction applies. Clears on read. Self-set to 1 on internal event.                                                                                                                                                      |

![Image](31_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_(EMAC)_artifacts/image_000324_36a8baaf414dcaa31ca4b21d2a4655311c22c5808feaa2960b99c1bba5d9df5a.png)

Table 28-380: EMAC\_TX\_URFL\_PCNT Register Fields

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                                                       |
|--------------------|------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 15:0 (R/NW)        | TXUNDRFLW  | Tx Underflow Error Packets. The EMAC_TX_URFL_PCNT.TXUNDRFLW field indicates the number of packets aborted because of packets underflow error. |

## Transmit Unicast Packets Good Bad Counter Register

The EMAC\_TX\_UCST\_PCNT\_GB register provides the number of good and bad unicast packets transmitted by the EMAC module.

![Image](31_Ethernet_Media_Access_Controller_(EMAC)_artifacts/image_000325_d2f322bee2bbc8f228a0f4ed1a29e7be46b8e2dfe4ee7ff181c7bfa307db9496.png)

Table 28-381: EMAC\_TX\_UCST\_PCNT\_GB Register Fields

| Bit No. (Access)   | Bit Name   | Description/Enumeration                                                                                    |
|--------------------|------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 15:0               | TXUCASTGB  | Tx Unicast Packets Good Bad.                                                                               |
| (R/NW)             |            | The EMAC_TX_UCST_PCNT_GB.TXUCASTGB field indicates the number of good and bad unicast packets transmitted. |

## Transmit VLAN Packets Good Counter Register

| 15:0               | TXVLANG    | Tx VLAN Packets Good.                                                                       |
| (R/NW)             |            | The EMAC_TX_VLAN_PCNT_G.TXVLANG field provides the number of good VLAN packets transmitted. |
